This document lists observations made by the FDA representative(s) during the inspection of your facility. They are inspectional observations, and do not represent a final
Agency determination regarding your compliance. If you have an objection regarding an observation, or have implemented, or plan to implement, corrective action in
response to an observation, you may discuss the objection or action with the FDA representative(s) during the inspection or submit this information to FDA at the address
above. If you have any questions, please contact FDA at the phone number and address above.
The observations noted in this Form FDA­483 are not an exhaustive listing of objectionable conditions. Under the law, your firm is responsible for conducting internal self­
audits to identify and correct any and all violations of the quality system requirements.

Quality System
OBSERVATION 1

2/12
The quality control unit lacks authority to fully investigate errors that have occurred.
The Quality Unit and Senior Management failed to assure all drug products distributed have the safety, identity, quality, and purity
that they are represented to possess. The Quality Unit failed to: review electronic data as part of batch release, review computer
audit trails in the Waters Empower Data Acquisition System and provide adequate training to analytical chemists. These practices
led to the Quality Unit releasing batches of drug products which failed to meet in­process, finished product and stability
specifications. These practices also led to the submission of erroneous data in Annual Reports and Prior Approval Supplement #
004, for ANDA 75­838, which requested discontinuance of Blend Uniformity testing for Propoxyphene Napsylate and
Acetaminophen 100mg/650 mg Tablets. The lack of Quality oversight resulted in: the ceasing of manufacturing on 5/13/05
5/19/05, the ceasing of distribution of all drug products on 5/26/05 5/13/05, the recall of all batches (3,184) of drug products and
the withdrawal of at least five Abbreviated New Drug Applications.
 
OBSERVATION 2
Drug products failing to meet established standards, specifications, and quality control criteria are not rejected.
Samples of drug products were routinely resampled, and re­injected or reprocessed in the [REDACTION] 
System during testing in the QC Laboratory when out of specification (OOS) results were obtained. There were no Laboratory
Investigations into OOS results or notebook documentation available to explain the re­injection or retesting of in­process, finished
product and stability samples which did not meet specifications. The OOS results were not reported and within specification
results from reprocessed or re­injected samples were reported on: In­Process Specification, Product Specification and Stability
Study Specification Release Reports and Stability Summary Reports.

observations.observation_text: The Quality Control Unit and Senior Management failed to exercise their responsibilities to assure that drug products distributed have the safety, identity, quality, and purity they are represented to possess.
evidence_list: The Quality Control Unit failed to review electronic data as part of batch release and failed to review computer audit trails in the Waters Empower Data Acquisition System.

Analytical chemists were not provided adequate training in Quality Control procedures, such as SOP # QC-011-03, 'Laboratory Deviation Investigations,' and SOP # QC-021-06, 'Acceptance/Rejection Criteria for OOS Analytical Test Results.' This lack of training contributed to the non-reporting of out-of-specification (OOS) results.

The firm's SOP # QC-022-04, 'Laboratory Records,' effective June 25, 2004, specified numerically ordered notebooks and a maintained log. However, notebook issuance logs showed large, unaccounted-for gaps in the numbering of notebooks issued. Additionally, the procedure for notebook issuance, as described by management (indicating a notebook request form was to be used), was not described in the available written procedure.

SOP Method Number I-037, 'General Guidelines for sample Logging for Analytical Laboratory using [REDACTION] software,' approved October 18, 2000, did not include procedures and responsibilities for personnel authorized to enter samples into the [REDACTION] database. Furthermore, forms required by the SOP to authorize the addition or deletion of groups, items, samples, and users to the [REDACTION] system were not used.

There was no Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) describing the use of 'special samples' (SP) tested in the Analytical Laboratory, nor were they listed as a group in the [REDACTION] procedure. For example, special samples (SP 04-101 dated April 24, 2004, and SP04-101 dated April 26, 2004, each consisting of 6 tablets) were used to report L3 Dissolution results for stability sample #ST04-407 for Methylphenidate HCl ER Tablets 20mg, Lot # 303087A, 9-month RT.

These systemic failures led to the Quality Control Unit releasing batches of drug products which failed to meet in-process, finished product, and stability specifications, resulting in the recall of all 3,184 batches of drug products and the withdrawal of at least five Abbreviated New Drug Applications.
observations.source_notes_excerpt: The quality control unit lacks authority to fully investigate errors that have occurred. The Quality Unit and Senior Management failed to assure all drug products distributed have the safety, identity, quality, and purity that they are represented to possess. The Quality Unit failed to: review electronic data as part of batch release, review computer audit trails in the Waters Empower Data Acquisition System and provide adequate training to analytical chemists... The lack of Quality oversight resulted in: the ceasing of manufacturing on 5/13/05 5/19/05, the ceasing of distribution of all drug products on 5/26/05 5/13/05, the recall of all batches (3,184) of drug products and the withdrawal of at least five Abbreviated New Drug Applications... Employees are not given training in current good manufacturing practices and written procedures required by current good manufacturing practice regulations. QC Laboratory analysts were not routinely trained in Quality Control procedures such as SOP # QC-011-03, Laboratory Deviation Investigations and SOP # QC-021-06... The responsibilities and procedures applicable to the quality control unit are not in writing and fully followed. a. The Laboratory Records SOP # QC-022-04... b. SOP Method Number I-037... c. There was no SOP describing the use of (SP) special samples...

observations.observation_text: Laboratory records do not include complete data derived from all tests, examinations, and assays necessary to assure compliance with established specifications and standards, and drug products failing to meet established standards are not rejected.
evidence_list: Samples of drug products were routinely resampled, re-injected, or reprocessed in the [REDACTION] System during testing in the QC Laboratory when out-of-specification (OOS) results were obtained. Within-specification results from these reprocessed or re-injected samples were then reported on In-Process Specification, Product Specification, and Stability Study Specification Release Reports.

Laboratory investigations were not conducted when OOS results were generated during in-process, finished product, and stability testing, despite the firm's Quality Control Procedure, SOP # QC-021-06, 'Acceptance/Rejection Criteria for OOS Analytical Test Results,' requiring such investigations. Examples include, but are not limited to, OOS results for Acetaminophen & Codeine Phosphate Tablet, Batch 502022 (in-process blend uniformity); Atenolol 25 mg Tablet, Validation Batch 408107B (3-month RT stability dissolution); and Propoxyphene Napsylate and APAP Tablets, 100/650mg, Batch 310158 (in-process blend uniformity).

QC Laboratory notebooks and binders lacked complete data, including OOS results, chromatograms, sample weights, and processing methods. OOS results were substituted with passing results by Analysts and Supervisors through data manipulation, such as: cutting and pasting chromatogram headers for Dissolution Testing of Tablets D1 and D5 for Propoxyphene Napsylate and APAP Tablets, 100/650mg, Batch 303110A; changing original sample weights by an analyst until a passing result was obtained for Assay (A2) for Propoxyphene Napsylate and APAP Tablets, 100/650mg, Validation Batch 104026B; and changing processing methods by an analyst until a passing result was obtained for Acetaminophen & Codeine Phosphate Tablets, 300/30mg, Batch 407148.

Audits were not conducted of the [REDACTION] System used to run HPLC instruments, and sample injections, processing methods, and sample weights were not reviewed or verified for the accuracy of reported results during testing of in-process, finished product, and stability samples.

Written records of investigations, such as OOS Investigation # 04-00S-031 for Methylphenidate HCl ER Tablets 20 mg, 18-month stability lot 303087A, were incomplete. The investigation concluded original failing dissolution results (average of 24 tablets reported as 48.4% against a specification range of [REDACTION]) were invalid due to analyst technique, but lacked documentation to justify this invalidation, and corrective measures were not documented as completed.

Established laboratory control mechanisms for retesting and investigations were not followed. For example, an investigation was not issued prior to retesting for Lot 303087B (Methylphenidate HCl ER 18-month stability lot), as required by SOP # QC-011-03. Additionally, SOP # QC-006-01, 'Retesting and Resampling Analytical Control Laboratory,' was not followed for Methylphenidate HCl ER 18-month stability lot 303087A regarding documentation of the number of retests and chemist involvement. Investigation 04-OOS-031 exceeded the 30-working-day completion timeframe required by procedure.

observations.observation_text: Annual reports and supplements submitted to the Agency did not include reports of investigations involving chemical or physical properties which, as new information, might affect FDA's previous conclusions about the safety or effectiveness of the drug, and Field Alert Reports were not submitted as required.
evidence_list: Annual Reports for Abbreviated New Drug Applications (ANDAs) submitted to FDA did not include out-of-specification (OOS) results; only passing data points were submitted. Examples include:

- Annual Report submitted August 24, 2004, for ANDA 75-838 (Propoxyphene Napsylate and APAP Tablets, 100/650mg, Batch 303110A), which omitted OOS dissolution results (D1=72.8%, D5=73.2%) and reported passing results (D1=98.5%, D5=96.9%).

- Annual Report submitted November 6, 2002, for ANDA 75-838 (Propoxyphene Napsylate and APAP Tablets, 100/650mg, Batch 104026B), which omitted an OOS assay result (A2=89.9%) and reported a passing result (A2=95.9%).

Prior Approval Supplement #004 for ANDA 75-838 (Propoxyphene Napsylate and APAP Tablets, 100/650mg), submitted March 16, 2004, to discontinue Blend Uniformity Testing, did not contain initial OOS results for a number of batches, only passing results. Examples include Batch 312015 (OOS Content Uniformity for Propoxyphene CU5 = 117.8%) and Batch 310158 (OOS Blend Uniformity for Propoxyphene TL1 = 238.5%, TR1 = 80.5%, and APAP TL1 = 218.9%).

Field Alert Reports (FA) were not routinely filed within three working days when distributed drug products did not meet ANDA specifications, particularly stability specifications. There is no Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) covering the issuance of Field Alerts. Examples include:
- Atenolol 25 mg Tablet, Validation Batch 408107A (ANDA 76-907): Original 3-month RT stability dissolution testing showed D5 = 83.7%, D6 = 83.8% (OOS), but no FA was submitted.
- Diphenoxylate HCl and Atropine Sulfate Tablet, Batch 301068A (ANDA 40-395): Original 21-month RT stability assay for Atropine showed A1 = 78.4%, A2 = 78.7% (OOS), but no FA was submitted.
Due to the submission of erroneous data, multiple ANDAs were withdrawn.

Field Alerts were not routinely filed when drug products did not meet the specifications... There is no SOP covering the issuance of Field Alerts. Field Alerts (FA) were not submitted when the following batches of drug products failed to meet stability specifications.

observations.observation_text: Control procedures are not established which validate the performance of those manufacturing processes that may be responsible for causing variability in the characteristics of in-process material and the drug product.
evidence_list: There is no assurance that results for in-process physical testing are recorded accurately. For example, the Pre-Validation batch record (TB-110) for Hydrocodone Bitartrate and Acetaminophen Tablets, USP 5mg/325mg, showed an incorrect tablet thickness specification range (0.308” to 0.358”) that was crossed out and replaced with a handwritten correct range of [REDACTION]. The Research and Development (R&D) In-Process Data Sheet for this batch showed the thickness of 60 tablets to be within a range (0.330” and 0.334”) that corresponded to the incorrectly written specification.

Manufacturing investigations into rejected batches of drug products did not include an evaluation of the validated manufacturing process. For example, Manufacturing Investigations 04-008 (for batch 310004) and 05-001 (for batch 411021) for Methylphenidate ER 20 mg Tablets did not include such an evaluation, despite 7 of 9 batches (78%) manufactured between May 2003 and November 2004 being investigated due to initial OOS or out-of-trend results.
There is no assurance that manufacturing processes for drug products are validated, as out-of-specification (OOS) results were generated but not reported for validation batches. Examples include:
- Atenolol 25 mg Tablet, Validation Batch 408107A: 3-month RT stability dissolution showed D5 = 83.7%, D6 = 83.8% (OOS), but 98.9% and 98.7% were reported.
- Propoxyphene Napsylate and APAP Tablets, 100/650mg, Validation Batch 104026B: 6-month RT stability assay for Propoxyphene showed A2 = 89.9% (OOS), but 95.9% was reported.

The quality control unit lacks authority to fully investigate errors that have occurred.
The Quality Unit and Senior Management failed to assure all drug products distributed have the safety, identity, quality, and purity
that they are represented to possess. The Quality Unit failed to: review electronic data as part of batch release, review computer
audit trails in the Waters Empower Data Acquisition System and provide adequate training to analytical chemists. These practices
led to the Quality Unit releasing batches of drug products which failed to meet in­process, finished product and stability
specifications. These practices also led to the submission of erroneous data in Annual Reports and Prior Approval Supplement #
004, for ANDA 75­838, which requested discontinuance of Blend Uniformity testing for Propoxyphene Napsylate and
Acetaminophen 100mg/650 mg Tablets. The lack of Quality oversight resulted in: the ceasing of manufacturing on 5/13/05
5/19/05, the ceasing of distribution of all drug products on 5/26/05 5/13/05, the recall of all batches (3,184) of drug products and
the withdrawal of at least five Abbreviated New Drug Applications.
 
OBSERVATION 2
Drug products failing to meet established standards, specifications, and quality control criteria are not rejected.

System during testing in the QC Laboratory when out of specification (OOS) results were obtained. There were no Laboratory

results from reprocessed or re­injected samples were reported on: In­Process Specification, Product Specification and Stability
Study Specification Release Reports and Stability Summary Reports.

Written records are not made of investigations into unexplained discrepancies and the failure of a batch or any of its components

manufacturing practice regulations.

Written records of investigations into unexplained discrepancies and the failure of a batch or any of its components to meet

OOS Investigation # 04­00S­031, for Methylphenidate HCl ER Tablets 20 mg 18 month stability lot 303087A was initiated due to
dissolution failing results. The specification required the average of 24 tablets to be within the range of [REDACTION] at the L3, 1
hour dissolution time point. The average of the 24 tablets was reported to be 48.4% with a minimum result of 45.8% and a
maximum of 50.2%. The investigation was found to be incomplete. The investigation concluded that the original failing results
were invalid due to an analyst technique issue. There was no documentation provided within the investigation or within the analyst
notebook to justify invalidating the failing dissolution results. Although corrective measures were identified in the investigation,
there was no documentation to show that the corrective measures had been completed. Additionally, there was no review of data
acquired by the same analysts for the same tests for other lots of the same product.

18M Dissolution stability analysis found that the original L3 testing results were within specification. Two months after the
analysis of 24 tablets for Lot 303087B for 18M stability, 6 more tablets were tested. The results from the final analysis of the 6
tablets were reported as 18 M Dissolution results.
b. SOP # QC­006­01 Retesting and Resampling Analytical Control Laboratory, effective 8/27/03 was not followed for
Methylphenidate HCl ER18M stability lot 303087A:
1. There was no documentation of the number of retests to be performed as required by the SOP. The SOP required the
number of retest to be documented prior to initiating testing to establish a definite limit beyond which no additional testing
would be permitted.
2. The procedure required retests to be conducted by the original chemist and a second chemist, where the second
chemist conducts at least 60% of the tests, or by two chemists, neither of which being the chemist producing the original
result. Retests were not carried out by the original chemist and a second chemist. Additionally, the test was not carried
out by two chemists other than the original chemist.
3. Investigation 04­OOS­031, initiated 12/8/04 and completed 2/18/05, exceeded 30 working days. The procedure required
investigations to be completed in a brief time frame not to exceed 30 working days from the start of the investigation.

specification of [REDACTION] during compression on 10/15/01. The Research and Development (R&D) In­Process Data

observations.observation_text: The quality control unit lacks the responsibility and authority to approve or reject all drug products, and to assure that drug products meet the safety, identity, strength, quality, and purity characteristics they are purported to possess. This failure of the Quality Control Unit and Senior Management to assure product quality led to the distribution of drug products that did not meet specifications and the submission of erroneous data to the Agency.
evidence_list: The Quality Control Unit failed to review electronic data as part of batch release.
The Quality Control Unit failed to review computer audit trails in the Waters Empower Data Acquisition System.

These practices led to the Quality Unit releasing batches of drug products which failed to meet in-process, finished product, and stability specifications, as further detailed in Observations 2, 3, and 4.
These practices also led to the submission of erroneous data in Annual Reports and Prior Approval Supplement #004 for ANDA 75-838.
The lack of Quality oversight resulted in the recall of 3,184 batches of drug products and the withdrawal of at least five Abbreviated New Drug Applications.
observations.source_notes_excerpt: The quality control unit lacks authority to fully investigate errors that have occurred. The Quality Unit and Senior Management failed to assure all drug products distributed have the safety, identity, quality, and purity that they are represented to possess. The Quality Unit failed to: review electronic data as part of batch release, review computer audit trails in the Waters Empower Data Acquisition System and provide adequate training to analytical chemists. These practices led to the Quality Unit releasing batches of drug products which failed to meet in-process, finished product and stability specifications. These practices also led to the submission of erroneous data in Annual Reports and Prior Approval Supplement # 004, for ANDA 75-838, which requested discontinuance of Blend Uniformity testing for Propoxyphene Napsylate and Acetaminophen 100mg/650 mg Tablets. The lack of Quality oversight resulted in: the ceasing of manufacturing on 5/13/05-5/19/05, the ceasing of distribution of all drug products on 5/26/05-5/13/05, the recall of all batches (3,184) of drug products and the withdrawal of at least five Abbreviated New Drug Applications.

observations.observation_text: Drug products failing to meet established standards, specifications, and quality control criteria are not rejected. This practice allows the release of drug products that may not meet their established quality specifications, potentially impacting patient safety and product efficacy.
evidence_list: During testing in the Quality Control Laboratory, samples of drug products were routinely resampled, re-injected, or reprocessed in the [REDACTION] System when out-of-specification (OOS) results were obtained.

The original OOS results were not reported. Instead, within-specification results from reprocessed or re-injected samples were reported on In-Process Specification, Product Specification, Stability Study Specification Release Reports, and Stability Summary Reports.
For example:

- Acetaminophen & Codeine Phosphate Tablet, Batch 502022, In-Process Blend Uniformity Testing: An original OOS result for Codeine Phosphate % RSD of 5.4% (Specification: [REDACTION]) was obtained, but a result of 3.8% was reported.

- Atenolol 25 mg Tablet, Validation Batch 408107A, 3-month Room Temperature Stability Sample: Original OOS Dissolution results of D5=83.7% and D6=83.8% (Specification: NLT [REDACTION]) were obtained, but results of D5=98.9% and D6=98.7% were reported.

- Propoxyphene Napsylate and APAP Tablets, Batch 310158, In-Process Blend Uniformity Testing: Original OOS results for Propoxyphene of TL1=238.5% and TR1=80.5%; APAP TL1=218.9% (Specification: [REDACTION]) were obtained, but results of Propoxyphene TL1=103.2%, TR1=104.0%; APAP TL1=105.6% were reported.
observations.source_notes_excerpt: Drug products failing to meet established standards, specifications, and quality control criteria are not rejected. Samples of drug products were routinely resampled, and re-injected or reprocessed in the [REDACTION] System during testing in the QC Laboratory when out of specification (OOS) results were obtained. There were no Laboratory Investigations into OOS results or notebook documentation available to explain the re-injection or retesting of in-process, finished product and stability samples which did not meet specifications. The OOS results were not reported and within specification results from reprocessed or re-injected samples were reported on: In-Process Specification, Product Specification and Stability Study Specification Release Reports and Stability Summary Reports. Examples of drug products which were released with OOS values are listed below. [Table of 18 examples follows, with specific data for Acetaminophen & Codeine Phosphate Tablet, Batch 502022; Atenolol 25 mg Tablet, Validation Batch 408107A; Propoxyphene Napsylate and APAP Tablets, Batch 310158 used in evidence list].

observations.observation_text: Laboratory records do not include complete data derived from all tests, examinations, and assays necessary to assure compliance with established specifications and standards. The lack of complete and accurate laboratory records, including the substitution of OOS results with passing data, compromises the integrity of analytical testing and prevents the firm from accurately determining if drug products meet their established specifications.
evidence_list: Quality Control (QC) Laboratory notebooks and binders lacked complete data from all analytical testing conducted. Laboratory records did not include all data such as out-of-specification (OOS) results, original chromatograms, original sample weights, and original processing methods.
OOS results were substituted with passing results by Analysts and Supervisors. This substitution of data was performed by:

- Cutting and pasting chromatogram headers to make all sample injections appear in sequence for Dissolution Testing of Propoxyphene Napsylate and APAP Tablets, 100/650mg, Batch 303110A (Tablets D1 and D5).

- Changing sample weights by the analyst until a passing result was obtained for Assay (A2) of Propoxyphene Napsylate and APAP Tablets, 100/650mg, Batch 104026B (Validation Batch). The original sample weights were not recorded in the notebook.

- Changing processing methods by the analyst until a passing result was obtained for Acetaminophen & Codeine Phosphate Tablets, 300/30mg, Batch 407148. The original processing method was not recorded in the laboratory notebook.
Unreported OOS results were found in electronic data files for products and batches listed in FDA-483, point #2, but were not documented in the corresponding laboratory records.
observations.source_notes_excerpt: Laboratory records do not include complete data derived from all tests, examinations and assay necessary to assure compliance with established specifications and standards. The QC Laboratory notebooks and binders lacked data from all analytical testing conducted in the QC Laboratory. Laboratory records did not include all data such as out of specification (OOS) results, chromatograms, sample weights, and processing methods. OOS results were substituted with passing results by Analysts and Supervisors. The substitution of data was performed by cutting and pasting of chromatograms, substituting vials, changing sample weights and changing processing methods. For Example: Products and batches listed in FDA-483, point # 2: OOS results not documented in laboratory records. Unreported OOS results found in electronic data files. Propoxyphene Napsylate and APAP Tablets, 100/650mg, Batch 303110A: Changed chromatogram headers by cutting and pasting, so during review all sample injections would appear to be in sequence, for Dissolution Testing of Tablets D1 and D5. Propoxyphene Napsylate and APAP Tablets, 100/650mg, Batch 104026B Validation Batch: Original Sample Weights not recorded in notebook. Sample weights were changed by the analyst until a passing result was obtained for Assay (A2). Acetaminophen & Codeine Phosphate Tablets, 300/30mg, Batch 407148: Processing methods changed by analyst until the processing method resulted in a passing result. Original processing method not recorded in laboratory notebook.

observations.observation_text: Written records are not made of investigations into unexplained discrepancies and the failure of a batch or any of its components to meet specifications. The failure to thoroughly investigate OOS results prevents the identification of root causes for quality failures, allowing for the potential recurrence of issues and the release of drug products that do not meet established specifications.
evidence_list: Laboratory investigations were not conducted when out-of-specification (OOS) results were generated during in-process, finished product, and stability testing of drug products.
Examples of batches where OOS results were generated and not investigated include, but are not limited to:
- Acetaminophen & Codeine Phosphate Tablet, Batch 502022, In-Process Blend Uniformity Testing, where an original OOS result for Codeine Phosphate % RSD of 5.4% was obtained.
- Atenolol 25 mg Tablet, Validation Batch 408107A, 3-month Room Temperature Stability Sample, where original OOS Dissolution results of D5=83.7% and D6=83.8% were obtained.

- Propoxyphene Napsylate and APAP Tablets, Batch 310158, In-Process Blend Uniformity Testing, where original OOS results for Propoxyphene of TL1=238.5% and TR1=80.5%, and APAP of TL1=218.9% were obtained.

The firm's Quality Control Procedure, SOP # QC-021-06, 'Acceptance/Rejection Criteria for OOS Analytical Test Results,' requires an investigation be conducted when OOS results are generated, but this procedure was not followed.

OOS Investigation # 04-00S-031, for Methylphenidate HCl ER Tablets 20 mg, 18-month stability lot 303087A, was initiated due to failing dissolution results. The investigation concluded that the original failing results were invalid due to an analyst technique issue, but no documentation was provided within the investigation or the analyst notebook to justify invalidating the results. Additionally, there was no documentation to show that identified corrective measures had been completed, nor was there a review of data acquired by the same analysts for the same tests for other lots of the same product.
observations.source_notes_excerpt: Written records are not made of investigations into unexplained discrepancies and the failure of a batch or any of its components to meet specifications. Laboratory investigations were not conducted when out of specification (OOS) results were generated during in-process, finished product and stability testing of drug products. Examples of batches where OOS results were generated and not investigated are included in FDA-483, point # 2. Quality Control Procedure, SOP # QC-021-06, Acceptance/Rejection Criteria for OOS Analytical Test Results, requires an investigation be conducted when OOS results are generated. OOS Investigation # 04-00S-031, for Methylphenidate HCl ER Tablets 20 mg 18 month stability lot 303087A was initiated due to dissolution failing results. The specification required the average of 24 tablets to be within the range of [REDACTION] at the L3, 1 hour dissolution time point. The average of the 24 tablets was reported to be 48.4% with a minimum result of 45.8% and a maximum of 50.2%. The investigation was found to be incomplete. The investigation concluded that the original failing results were invalid due to an analyst technique issue. There was no documentation provided within the investigation or within the analyst notebook to justify invalidating the failing dissolution results. Although corrective measures were identified in the investigation, there was no documentation to show that the corrective measures had been completed. Additionally, there was no review of data acquired by the same analysts for the same tests for other lots of the same product.

observations.observation_text: Annual reports submitted to the Agency do not include reports of investigations involving chemical or physical properties which, as new information, might affect FDA's previous conclusions about the safety or effectiveness of the drug, and Field Alert Reports were not submitted within three working days of receipt of information concerning a failure of one or more distributed batches of a drug to meet the specifications established for it in the application. The submission of erroneous and incomplete data to the FDA, and the failure to submit timely Field Alert Reports, prevented the Agency from making informed conclusions about the safety and effectiveness of the drug products and from being promptly informed of significant quality issues with distributed drug products, potentially delaying necessary regulatory actions to protect public health.
evidence_list: Annual Reports for Abbreviated New Drug Applications (ANDAs) were submitted to FDA without including out-of-specification (OOS) results; only passing data points were submitted. For example:

- The Annual Report submitted on August 24, 2004, for ANDA 75-838 (Propoxyphene Napsylate and APAP Tablets, 100/650mg, Batch 303110A, 12-month Room Temperature Stability Sample) reported Dissolution results of D1=98.5% and D5=96.9%, while original OOS results were D1=72.8% and D5=73.2% (Specification: NLT [REDACTION]).

Prior Approval Supplement #004 for ANDA 75-838 (Propoxyphene Napsylate and APAP Tablets, 100/650mg), submitted on March 16, 2004, to provide for the discontinuance of Blend Uniformity Testing, did not contain initial OOS results for a number of batches; only passing results were submitted. For example, for Batch 312015, Finished Product Content Uniformity, the supplement reported a range of 102.8%-108.2% for Propoxyphene, while an original OOS result of CU5=117.8% (Specification: 85%-115%) was obtained.

Field Alerts were not routinely filed when drug products did not meet the specifications listed in their ANDAs. The firm does not have a Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) covering the issuance of Field Alerts.

Field Alerts were not submitted for distributed batches of drug products that failed to meet stability specifications, such as Atenolol 25 mg Tablet, Validation Batch 408107A (ANDA 76-907), 3-month Room Temperature Stability Sample, where original OOS Dissolution results of D5=83.7% and D6=83.8% (Specification: NLT [REDACTION]) were obtained.
observations.source_notes_excerpt: An annual report did not include reports of investigations involving chemical or physical properties which, as new information, might affect FDA's previous conclusions about the safety or effectiveness of the drug. a. Annual Reports for ANDA’s that were submitted to FDA did not include out of specification (OOS) results. Only passing data points were submitted. Due to the submission of erroneous data the following ANDA’s were withdrawn. [Examples follow, including Propoxyphene Napsylate and APAP Tablets, 100/650mg, Batch 303110A]. b. Prior Approval Supplement #004 for ANDA 75-838, Propoxyphene Napsylate and APAP Tablets, 100/650mg, was submitted on 3/16/04 to provide for the discontinuance of Blend Uniformity Testing. This supplement was approved 9/23/04. The test data submitted for Blend Uniformity and Content Uniformity did not contain initial OOS results for a number of batches, only passing results were submitted. Due to the submission of erroneous data the ANDA was withdrawn. OOS results for these batches are listed below. [Examples follow, including Batch 312015]. An NDA-Field Alert Report was not submitted within three working days of receipt of information concerning a failure of one or more distributed batches of a drug to meet the specifications established for it in the application. Field Alerts were not routinely filed when drug products did not meet the specifications listed in the Abbreviated New Drug Application (ANDA). There is no SOP covering the issuance of Field Alerts. Field Alerts (FA) were not submitted when the following batches of drug products failed to meet stability specifications. [Examples follow, including Atenolol 25 mg Tablet, Validation Batch 408107A].

observations.observation_text: Employees are not given training in current good manufacturing practices and written procedures required by current good manufacturing practice regulations. Inadequate training of analytical personnel increases the risk of non-compliance with established procedures and regulatory requirements, leading to unreliable test results and potentially compromising drug product quality.
evidence_list: Quality Control (QC) Laboratory analysts were not routinely trained in Quality Control procedures such as SOP # QC-011-03, 'Laboratory Deviation Investigations,' and SOP # QC-021-06, 'Acceptance/Rejection Criteria for OOS Analytical Test Results.'
This lack of training and oversight by management contributed to the non-reporting of OOS results in the QC Laboratory.
observations.source_notes_excerpt: Employees are not given training in current good manufacturing practices and written procedures required by current good manufacturing practice regulations. QC Laboratory analysts were not routinely trained in Quality Control procedures such as SOP # QC-011-03, Laboratory Deviation Investigations and SOP # QC-021-06, Acceptance/Rejection Criteria for OOS Analytical Test Results. This lack of training and oversight by management contributed to the non-reporting of OOS results in the QC Laboratory.

2/12
The quality control unit lacks authority to fully investigate errors that have occurred.
The Quality Unit and Senior Management failed to assure all drug products distributed have the safety, identity, quality, and purity
that they are represented to possess. The Quality Unit failed to: review electronic data as part of batch release, review computer
audit trails in the Waters Empower Data Acquisition System and provide adequate training to analytical chemists. These practices
led to the Quality Unit releasing batches of drug products which failed to meet in­process, finished product and stability
specifications. These practices also led to the submission of erroneous data in Annual Reports and Prior Approval Supplement #
004, for ANDA 75­838, which requested discontinuance of Blend Uniformity testing for Propoxyphene Napsylate and
Acetaminophen 100mg/650 mg Tablets. The lack of Quality oversight resulted in: the ceasing of manufacturing on 5/13/05
5/19/05, the ceasing of distribution of all drug products on 5/26/05 5/13/05, the recall of all batches (3,184) of drug products and
the withdrawal of at least five Abbreviated New Drug Applications.
 
OBSERVATION 2
Drug products failing to meet established standards, specifications, and quality control criteria are not rejected.
Samples of drug products were routinely resampled, and re­injected or reprocessed in the [REDACTION] 
System during testing in the QC Laboratory when out of specification (OOS) results were obtained. There were no Laboratory
Investigations into OOS results or notebook documentation available to explain the re­injection or retesting of in­process, finished
product and stability samples which did not meet specifications. The OOS results were not reported and within specification
results from reprocessed or re­injected samples were reported on: In­Process Specification, Product Specification and Stability
Study Specification Release Reports and Stability Summary Reports.

OBSERVATION 7
Written records are not made of investigations into unexplained discrepancies and the failure of a batch or any of its components
to meet specifications.
Laboratory investigations were not conducted when out of specification (OOS) results were generated during in­process, finished
product and stability testing of drug products. Examples of batches where OOS results were generated and not investigated are
included in FDA­483, point # 2. Quality Control Procedure, SOP # QC­021­06, Acceptance/Rejection Criteria for OOS Analytical
Test Results, requires an investigation be conducted when OOS results are generated.
 
OBSERVATION 8
Employees are not given training in current good manufacturing practices and written procedures required by current good
manufacturing practice regulations.
QC Laboratory analysts were not routinely trained in Quality Control procedures such as SOP # QC­011­03, Laboratory Deviation
Investigations and SOP # QC­021­06, Acceptance/Rejection Criteria for OOS Analytical Test Results. This lack of training and
oversight by management contributed to the non­reporting of OOS results in the QC Laboratory.
 
OBSERVATION 9
Written records of investigations into unexplained discrepancies and the failure of a batch or any of its components to meet
specifications do not always include the conclusions and followup.
OOS Investigation # 04­00S­031, for Methylphenidate HCl ER Tablets 20 mg 18 month stability lot 303087A was initiated due to
dissolution failing results. The specification required the average of 24 tablets to be within the range of [REDACTION] at the L3, 1
hour dissolution time point. The average of the 24 tablets was reported to be 48.4% with a minimum result of 45.8% and a
maximum of 50.2%. The investigation was found to be incomplete. The investigation concluded that the original failing results
were invalid due to an analyst technique issue. There was no documentation provided within the investigation or within the analyst
notebook to justify invalidating the failing dissolution results. Although corrective measures were identified in the investigation,
there was no documentation to show that the corrective measures had been completed. Additionally, there was no review of data
acquired by the same analysts for the same tests for other lots of the same product.

Methylphenidate HCl ER18M stability lot 303087A:
1. There was no documentation of the number of retests to be performed as required by the SOP. The SOP required the
number of retest to be documented prior to initiating testing to establish a definite limit beyond which no additional testing
would be permitted.
2. The procedure required retests to be conducted by the original chemist and a second chemist, where the second
chemist conducts at least 60% of the tests, or by two chemists, neither of which being the chemist producing the original
result. Retests were not carried out by the original chemist and a second chemist. Additionally, the test was not carried
out by two chemists other than the original chemist.

Control procedures are not established which validate the performance of those manufacturing processes that may be
responsible for causing variability in the characteristics of in­process material and the drug product.
a. There is no assurance that results for in­process physical testing are recorded accurately. For example, the Pre­Validation
batch record (TB­110) for Hydrocodone Bitartrate and Acetaminophen Tablets, USP 5mg/325mg shows the specification for
tablet thickness range as 0.308” to 0.358”; this range was crossed out and the correct range of [REDACTION] was
handwritten in the batch record. The in­process tablet thickness results show all tablets were within the corrected thickness
specification of [REDACTION] during compression on 10/15/01. The Research and Development (R&D) In­Process Data
Sheet shows the thickness of 60 tablets to be within a thickness range of 0.330” and 0.334” which corresponds to the tablet
thickness specification which was incorrectly written on the Master Batch Record. Retains from this batch were tested on
6/10/05, and the results show the thickness of the tablets were between [REDACTION] , which was the correct specification
that was handwritten on the Master Batch Record.
b. Manufacturing Investigations into rejected batches of drug products did not include an evaluation of the validated
manufacturing process. For example, seven of nine batches (78%) of Methylphenidate ER 20 mg Tablets, manufactured
between May 2003 and November 2004 were investigated in the laboratory, due to initial OOS results or out of trend results.

validated manufacturing process for Methylphenidate ER 20 mg Tablets.
c. There is no assurance that manufacturing processes for drug products are validated in that out of specification (OOS) results

observations.observation_text: Laboratory records do not include complete data derived from all tests, examinations, and assays necessary to assure compliance with established specifications and standards, as out-of-specification (OOS) results were substituted with passing results by analysts and supervisors through data manipulation.
evidence_list: The QC Laboratory notebooks and binders lacked data from all analytical testing conducted in the QC Laboratory.
Laboratory records did not include all data such as out of specification (OOS) results, chromatograms, sample weights, and processing methods.
OOS results were substituted with passing results by Analysts and Supervisors.
The substitution of data was performed by cutting and pasting of chromatograms, substituting vials, changing sample weights and changing processing methods.
For Propoxyphene Napsylate and APAP Tablets, 100/650mg, Batch 303110A, chromatogram headers were changed by cutting and pasting for Dissolution Testing of Tablets D1 and D5 to appear in sequence.

For Propoxyphene Napsylate and APAP Tablets, 100/650mg, Batch 104026B Validation Batch, original sample weights were not recorded in the notebook and were changed by the analyst until a passing result was obtained for Assay (A2).

For Acetaminophen & Codeine Phosphate Tablets, 300/30mg, Batch 407148, processing methods were changed by the analyst until a passing result was obtained, and the original processing method was not recorded.

observations.observation_text: Written records of investigations into unexplained discrepancies and the failure of a batch or any of its components to meet specifications do not always include the conclusions and followup, as demonstrated by an incomplete OOS investigation for Methylphenidate HCl ER Tablets 20 mg.
evidence_list: OOS Investigation # 04-00S-031, for Methylphenidate HCl ER Tablets 20 mg 18 month stability lot 303087A was initiated due to dissolution failing results.
The investigation was found to be incomplete.
There was no documentation provided within the investigation or within the analyst notebook to justify invalidating the failing dissolution results.
There was no documentation to show that the corrective measures identified in the investigation had been completed.
There was no review of data acquired by the same analysts for the same tests for other lots of the same product.
observations.source_notes_excerpt: Written records of investigations into unexplained discrepancies and the failure of a batch or any of its components to meet specifications do not always include the conclusions and followup. OOS Investigation # 04-00S-031, for Methylphenidate HCl ER Tablets 20 mg 18 month stability lot 303087A was initiated due to dissolution failing results... The investigation was found to be incomplete. The investigation concluded that the original failing results were invalid due to an analyst technique issue. There was no documentation provided within the investigation or within the analyst notebook to justify invalidating the failing dissolution results. Although corrective measures were identified in the investigation, there was no documentation to show that the corrective measures had been completed. Additionally, there was no review of data acquired by the same analysts for the same tests for other lots of the same product.

response to an observation, you may discuss the objection or action with the FDA representative(s) during the inspection or submit this information to FDA at the address

The observations noted in this Form FDA­483 are not an exhaustive listing of objectionable conditions. Under the law, your firm is responsible for conducting internal self­

Quality System
OBSERVATION 1

2/12
The quality control unit lacks authority to fully investigate errors that have occurred.
The Quality Unit and Senior Management failed to assure all drug products distributed have the safety, identity, quality, and purity
that they are represented to possess. The Quality Unit failed to: review electronic data as part of batch release, review computer
audit trails in the Waters Empower Data Acquisition System and provide adequate training to analytical chemists. These practices
led to the Quality Unit releasing batches of drug products which failed to meet in­process, finished product and stability
specifications. These practices also led to the submission of erroneous data in Annual Reports and Prior Approval Supplement #
004, for ANDA 75­838, which requested discontinuance of Blend Uniformity testing for Propoxyphene Napsylate and
Acetaminophen 100mg/650 mg Tablets. The lack of Quality oversight resulted in: the ceasing of manufacturing on 5/13/05
5/19/05, the ceasing of distribution of all drug products on 5/26/05 5/13/05, the recall of all batches (3,184) of drug products and
the withdrawal of at least five Abbreviated New Drug Applications.
 
OBSERVATION 2
Drug products failing to meet established standards, specifications, and quality control criteria are not rejected.
Samples of drug products were routinely resampled, and re­injected or reprocessed in the [REDACTION] 
System during testing in the QC Laboratory when out of specification (OOS) results were obtained. There were no Laboratory
Investigations into OOS results or notebook documentation available to explain the re­injection or retesting of in­process, finished
product and stability samples which did not meet specifications. The OOS results were not reported and within specification
results from reprocessed or re­injected samples were reported on: In­Process Specification, Product Specification and Stability
Study Specification Release Reports and Stability Summary Reports.

Audits were not conducted of the [REDACTION] System used to run the HPLC instruments during analysis of drug products.
Sample injections, processing methods, and sample weights were not reviewed or verified for the accuracy of reported sample

OBSERVATION 7
Written records are not made of investigations into unexplained discrepancies and the failure of a batch or any of its components
to meet specifications.
Laboratory investigations were not conducted when out of specification (OOS) results were generated during in­process, finished
product and stability testing of drug products. Examples of batches where OOS results were generated and not investigated are
included in FDA­483, point # 2. Quality Control Procedure, SOP # QC­021­06, Acceptance/Rejection Criteria for OOS Analytical
Test Results, requires an investigation be conducted when OOS results are generated.
 
OBSERVATION 8
Employees are not given training in current good manufacturing practices and written procedures required by current good
manufacturing practice regulations.
QC Laboratory analysts were not routinely trained in Quality Control procedures such as SOP # QC­011­03, Laboratory Deviation
Investigations and SOP # QC­021­06, Acceptance/Rejection Criteria for OOS Analytical Test Results. This lack of training and
oversight by management contributed to the non­reporting of OOS results in the QC Laboratory.
 
OBSERVATION 9
Written records of investigations into unexplained discrepancies and the failure of a batch or any of its components to meet
specifications do not always include the conclusions and followup.
OOS Investigation # 04­00S­031, for Methylphenidate HCl ER Tablets 20 mg 18 month stability lot 303087A was initiated due to
dissolution failing results. The specification required the average of 24 tablets to be within the range of [REDACTION] at the L3, 1
hour dissolution time point. The average of the 24 tablets was reported to be 48.4% with a minimum result of 45.8% and a
maximum of 50.2%. The investigation was found to be incomplete. The investigation concluded that the original failing results
were invalid due to an analyst technique issue. There was no documentation provided within the investigation or within the analyst
notebook to justify invalidating the failing dissolution results. Although corrective measures were identified in the investigation,
there was no documentation to show that the corrective measures had been completed. Additionally, there was no review of data
acquired by the same analysts for the same tests for other lots of the same product.
 
OBSERVATION 10
The responsibilities and procedures applicable to the quality control unit are not in writing and fully followed.
a. The Laboratory Records SOP # QC­022­04 effective 6/25/04, specified numerically ordered notebooks will be issued and a
log maintained. Notebook issuance logs showed large gaps in numbering of notebooks issued, which were not accounted for
in the log. Additionally, the procedure for issuance of notebooks, as described by management, which indicated a notebook
request form was to be used, was not described in the procedure available.
b. SOP Method Number I­037, approved 10/18/00, General Guidelines for sample Logging for Analytical Laboratory using
[REDACTION] software did not include procedures and responsibilities to be followed by personnel authorized to enter
samples into the [REDACTION] database. According to management, authorized personnel included floor inspectors and
incoming inspectors. The SOP required the use of forms to authorize addition or deletion of groups, items, samples, and
users to the [REDACTION] system. Forms to be used to authorize the addition or deletion of groups, items, samples, and
users to the [REDACTION] system as specified by the SOP were not used.
c. There was no SOP describing the use of (SP) special samples tested in the Analytical Laboratory. Additionally, special
samples were not listed as a group in the [REDACTION] procedure. Special samples in the testing of Methylphenidate HCl

Established laboratory control mechanisms are not followed.
a. An Investigation was not issued prior to any retesting for Lot 303087B, Methylphenidate HCl ER 18M stability lot, as required
by procedure SOP # QC­011­03, Laboratory Deviation Investigation. Lot 303087B, Methylphenidate HCl ER Tablets 20 mg,
18M Dissolution stability analysis found that the original L3 testing results were within specification. Two months after the
analysis of 24 tablets for Lot 303087B for 18M stability, 6 more tablets were tested. The results from the final analysis of the 6
tablets were reported as 18 M Dissolution results.
b. SOP # QC­006­01 Retesting and Resampling Analytical Control Laboratory, effective 8/27/03 was not followed for
Methylphenidate HCl ER18M stability lot 303087A:
1. There was no documentation of the number of retests to be performed as required by the SOP. The SOP required the
number of retest to be documented prior to initiating testing to establish a definite limit beyond which no additional testing
would be permitted.
2. The procedure required retests to be conducted by the original chemist and a second chemist, where the second
chemist conducts at least 60% of the tests, or by two chemists, neither of which being the chemist producing the original
result. Retests were not carried out by the original chemist and a second chemist. Additionally, the test was not carried
out by two chemists other than the original chemist.
3. Investigation 04­OOS­031, initiated 12/8/04 and completed 2/18/05, exceeded 30 working days. The procedure required
investigations to be completed in a brief time frame not to exceed 30 working days from the start of the investigation.
Production System
 
OBSERVATION 12
Control procedures are not established which validate the performance of those manufacturing processes that may be
responsible for causing variability in the characteristics of in­process material and the drug product.
a. There is no assurance that results for in­process physical testing are recorded accurately. For example, the Pre­Validation
batch record (TB­110) for Hydrocodone Bitartrate and Acetaminophen Tablets, USP 5mg/325mg shows the specification for
tablet thickness range as 0.308” to 0.358”; this range was crossed out and the correct range of [REDACTION] was
handwritten in the batch record. The in­process tablet thickness results show all tablets were within the corrected thickness
specification of [REDACTION] during compression on 10/15/01. The Research and Development (R&D) In­Process Data
Sheet shows the thickness of 60 tablets to be within a thickness range of 0.330” and 0.334” which corresponds to the tablet
thickness specification which was incorrectly written on the Master Batch Record. Retains from this batch were tested on
6/10/05, and the results show the thickness of the tablets were between [REDACTION] , which was the correct specification
that was handwritten on the Master Batch Record.
b. Manufacturing Investigations into rejected batches of drug products did not include an evaluation of the validated
manufacturing process. For example, seven of nine batches (78%) of Methylphenidate ER 20 mg Tablets, manufactured
between May 2003 and November 2004 were investigated in the laboratory, due to initial OOS results or out of trend results.
Two of the seven lab investigations, resulted in the rejection of batches 411021 and 310004. Manufacturing Investigations,
04­008, for batch 310004, and Manufacturing Investigation 05­001, for batch, 411021 did not include an evaluation of the
validated manufacturing process for Methylphenidate ER 20 mg Tablets.
c. There is no assurance that manufacturing processes for drug products are validated in that out of specification (OOS) results
were generated, but not reported. Several examples are listed below.

observations.observation_text: Drug products failing to meet established standards, specifications, and quality control criteria were not rejected. Samples of drug products were routinely resampled, re-injected, or reprocessed in the [REDACTION] System during testing in the QC Laboratory when out-of-specification (OOS) results were obtained. The OOS results were not reported, and within-specification results from reprocessed or re-injected samples were reported on official release reports, leading to the release of drug products that failed to meet specifications.

observations.observation_text: Laboratory records do not include complete data derived from all tests, examinations, and assays necessary to assure compliance with established specifications and standards. Out-of-specification (OOS) results were substituted with passing results by analysts and supervisors through practices such as cutting and pasting chromatograms, substituting vials, changing sample weights, and changing processing methods.
evidence_list: The QC Laboratory notebooks and binders lacked data from all analytical testing conducted in the QC Laboratory.
Laboratory records did not include all data such as out of specification (OOS) results, chromatograms, sample weights, and processing methods.

OOS results were substituted with passing results by Analysts and Supervisors. The substitution of data was performed by cutting and pasting of chromatograms, substituting vials, changing sample weights and changing processing methods.
For Propoxyphene Napsylate and APAP Tablets, 100/650mg, Batch 303110A, chromatogram headers were changed by cutting and pasting for Dissolution Testing of Tablets D1 and D5.

For Propoxyphene Napsylate and APAP Tablets, 100/650mg, Batch 104026B, original sample weights were not recorded in the notebook, and sample weights were changed by the analyst until a passing result was obtained for Assay (A2).

For Acetaminophen & Codeine Phosphate Tablets, 300/30mg, Batch 407148, processing methods were changed by the analyst until the processing method resulted in a passing result, and the original processing method was not recorded in the laboratory notebook.

observations.observation_text: Written records are not made of investigations into unexplained discrepancies and the failure of a batch or any of its components to meet specifications. Laboratory investigations were not conducted when out-of-specification (OOS) results were generated during in-process, finished product, and stability testing of drug products, despite the firm's SOP # QC-021-06 requiring such investigations.
evidence_list: Laboratory investigations were not conducted when out of specification (OOS) results were generated during in-process, finished product and stability testing of drug products.
Examples of batches where OOS results were generated and not investigated are included in FDA-483, point # 2.

observations.observation_text: Employees are not given training in current good manufacturing practices and written procedures required by current good manufacturing practice regulations. QC Laboratory analysts were not routinely trained in Quality Control procedures such as SOP # QC-011-03, Laboratory Deviation Investigations, and SOP # QC-021-06, Acceptance/Rejection Criteria for OOS Analytical Test Results, which contributed to the non-reporting of OOS results.
evidence_list: QC Laboratory analysts were not routinely trained in Quality Control procedures such as SOP # QC-011-03, Laboratory Deviation Investigations and SOP # QC-021-06, Acceptance/Rejection Criteria for OOS Analytical Test Results.
This lack of training and oversight by management contributed to the non-reporting of OOS results in the QC Laboratory.

observations.observation_text: Written records of investigations into unexplained discrepancies and the failure of a batch or any of its components to meet specifications do not always include the conclusions and follow-up. For example, OOS Investigation # 04-00S-031 for Methylphenidate HCl ER Tablets 20 mg, 18 month stability lot 303087A, concluded that original failing dissolution results were invalid due to an analyst technique issue, but no documentation was provided to justify this invalidation. Additionally, there was no documentation to show that identified corrective measures had been completed, nor was there a review of data acquired by the same analysts for other lots of the same product.
evidence_list: OOS Investigation # 04-00S-031, for Methylphenidate HCl ER Tablets 20 mg 18 month stability lot 303087A was initiated due to dissolution failing results.

The investigation concluded that the original failing results were invalid due to an analyst technique issue. There was no documentation provided within the investigation or within the analyst notebook to justify invalidating the failing dissolution results.
Although corrective measures were identified in the investigation, there was no documentation to show that the corrective measures had been completed.
Additionally, there was no review of data acquired by the same analysts for the same tests for other lots of the same product.
observations.source_notes_excerpt: Written records of investigations into unexplained discrepancies and the failure of a batch or any of its components to meet specifications do not always include the conclusions and followup. OOS Investigation # 04-00S-031, for Methylphenidate HCl ER Tablets 20 mg 18 month stability lot 303087A was initiated due to dissolution failing results. The specification required the average of 24 tablets to be within the range of [REDACTION] at the L3, 1 hour dissolution time point. The average of the 24 tablets was reported to be 48.4% with a minimum result of 45.8% and a maximum of 50.2%. The investigation was found to be incomplete. The investigation concluded that the original failing results were invalid due to an analyst technique issue. There was no documentation provided within the investigation or within the analyst notebook to justify invalidating the failing dissolution results. Although corrective measures were identified in the investigation, there was no documentation to show that the corrective measures had been completed. Additionally, there was no review of data acquired by the same analysts for the same tests for other lots of the same product.

observations.observation_text: Established laboratory control mechanisms are not followed. observations.observation_text: Established laboratory control mechanisms are not followed. SOP # QC-006-01, Retesting and Resampling Analytical Control Laboratory, effective 8/27/03, was not followed for Methylphenidate HCl ER 18M stability lot 303087A. There was no documentation of the number of retests to be performed prior to initiating testing, and retests were not carried out by the original chemist and a second chemist, or by two chemists other than the original chemist, as required by the procedure.
evidence_list: SOP # QC-006-01 Retesting and Resampling Analytical Control Laboratory, effective 8/27/03 was not followed for Methylphenidate HCl ER18M stability lot 303087A.
There was no documentation of the number of retests to be performed as required by the SOP.

The procedure required retests to be conducted by the original chemist and a second chemist, where the second chemist conducts at least 60% of the tests, or by two chemists, neither of which being the chemist producing the original result.
Retests were not carried out by the original chemist and a second chemist. Additionally, the test was not carried out by two chemists other than the original chemist.
observations.source_notes_excerpt: b. observations.observation_text: There is no assurance that results for in-process physical testing are recorded accurately. For example, the Pre-Validation batch record (TB-110) for Hydrocodone Bitartrate and Acetaminophen Tablets, USP 5mg/325mg, showed an incorrect tablet thickness specification (0.308” to 0.358”) that was handwritten as corrected. The Research and Development (R&D) In-Process Data Sheet showed thickness results (0.330” and 0.334”) corresponding to the incorrect specification, while retains tested on 6/10/05 showed results within the corrected specification.
evidence_list: The Pre-Validation batch record (TB-110) for Hydrocodone Bitartrate and Acetaminophen Tablets, USP 5mg/325mg shows the specification for tablet thickness range as 0.308” to 0.358”; this range was crossed out and the correct range of [REDACTION] was handwritten in the batch record.

The Research and Development (R&D) In-Process Data Sheet shows the thickness of 60 tablets to be within a thickness range of 0.330” and 0.334” which corresponds to the tablet thickness specification which was incorrectly written on the Master Batch Record.

Retains from this batch were tested on 6/10/05, and the results show the thickness of the tablets were between [REDACTION] , which was the correct specification that was handwritten on the Master Batch Record.

This document lists observations made by the FDA representative(s) during the inspection of your facility. They are inspectional observations, and do not represent a final
Agency determination regarding your compliance. If you have an objection regarding an observation, or have implemented, or plan to implement, corrective action in
response to an observation, you may discuss the objection or action with the FDA representative(s) during the inspection or submit this information to FDA at the address
above. If you have any questions, please contact FDA at the phone number and address above.
The observations noted in this Form FDA­483 are not an exhaustive listing of objectionable conditions. Under the law, your firm is responsible for conducting internal self­
audits to identify and correct any and all violations of the quality system requirements.
DURING AN INSPECTION OF YOUR FIRM WE OBSERVED: 
Quality System
OBSERVATION 1

6/24/2016
ORA FOIA Electronic Reading Room > Able Laboratories, Inc., Cranberry, NJ, FDA 483 Inspectional Observations, dated 05/02­07/01/2005
http://www.fda.gov/aboutfda/centersoffices/officeofglobalregulatoryoperationsandpolicy/ora/oraelectronicreadingroom/ucm061813.htm
2/12
The quality control unit lacks authority to fully investigate errors that have occurred.
The Quality Unit and Senior Management failed to assure all drug products distributed have the safety, identity, quality, and purity
that they are represented to possess. The Quality Unit failed to: review electronic data as part of batch release, review computer
audit trails in the Waters Empower Data Acquisition System and provide adequate training to analytical chemists. These practices
led to the Quality Unit releasing batches of drug products which failed to meet in­process, finished product and stability
specifications. These practices also led to the submission of erroneous data in Annual Reports and Prior Approval Supplement #
004, for ANDA 75­838, which requested discontinuance of Blend Uniformity testing for Propoxyphene Napsylate and
Acetaminophen 100mg/650 mg Tablets. The lack of Quality oversight resulted in: the ceasing of manufacturing on 5/13/05
5/19/05, the ceasing of distribution of all drug products on 5/26/05 5/13/05, the recall of all batches (3,184) of drug products and
the withdrawal of at least five Abbreviated New Drug Applications.
 
OBSERVATION 2
Drug products failing to meet established standards, specifications, and quality control criteria are not rejected.
Samples of drug products were routinely resampled, and re­injected or reprocessed in the [REDACTION] 
System during testing in the QC Laboratory when out of specification (OOS) results were obtained. There were no Laboratory
Investigations into OOS results or notebook documentation available to explain the re­injection or retesting of in­process, finished
product and stability samples which did not meet specifications. The OOS results were not reported and within specification
results from reprocessed or re­injected samples were reported on: In­Process Specification, Product Specification and Stability
Study Specification Release Reports and Stability Summary Reports.

Audits were not conducted of the [REDACTION] System used to run the HPLC instruments during analysis of drug products.
Sample injections, processing methods, and sample weights were not reviewed or verified for the accuracy of reported sample
results during testing of in­process, finished product and stability samples.
 
OBSERVATION 7
Written records are not made of investigations into unexplained discrepancies and the failure of a batch or any of its components
to meet specifications.
Laboratory investigations were not conducted when out of specification (OOS) results were generated during in­process, finished
product and stability testing of drug products. Examples of batches where OOS results were generated and not investigated are
included in FDA­483, point # 2. Quality Control Procedure, SOP # QC­021­06, Acceptance/Rejection Criteria for OOS Analytical
Test Results, requires an investigation be conducted when OOS results are generated.
 
OBSERVATION 8
Employees are not given training in current good manufacturing practices and written procedures required by current good
manufacturing practice regulations.
QC Laboratory analysts were not routinely trained in Quality Control procedures such as SOP # QC­011­03, Laboratory Deviation
Investigations and SOP # QC­021­06, Acceptance/Rejection Criteria for OOS Analytical Test Results. This lack of training and
oversight by management contributed to the non­reporting of OOS results in the QC Laboratory.
 
OBSERVATION 9
Written records of investigations into unexplained discrepancies and the failure of a batch or any of its components to meet
specifications do not always include the conclusions and followup.
OOS Investigation # 04­00S­031, for Methylphenidate HCl ER Tablets 20 mg 18 month stability lot 303087A was initiated due to
dissolution failing results. The specification required the average of 24 tablets to be within the range of [REDACTION] at the L3, 1
hour dissolution time point. The average of the 24 tablets was reported to be 48.4% with a minimum result of 45.8% and a
maximum of 50.2%. The investigation was found to be incomplete. The investigation concluded that the original failing results
were invalid due to an analyst technique issue. There was no documentation provided within the investigation or within the analyst
notebook to justify invalidating the failing dissolution results. Although corrective measures were identified in the investigation,
there was no documentation to show that the corrective measures had been completed. Additionally, there was no review of data
acquired by the same analysts for the same tests for other lots of the same product.
 
OBSERVATION 10
The responsibilities and procedures applicable to the quality control unit are not in writing and fully followed.
a. The Laboratory Records SOP # QC­022­04 effective 6/25/04, specified numerically ordered notebooks will be issued and a
log maintained. Notebook issuance logs showed large gaps in numbering of notebooks issued, which were not accounted for
in the log. Additionally, the procedure for issuance of notebooks, as described by management, which indicated a notebook
request form was to be used, was not described in the procedure available.
b. SOP Method Number I­037, approved 10/18/00, General Guidelines for sample Logging for Analytical Laboratory using
[REDACTION] software did not include procedures and responsibilities to be followed by personnel authorized to enter
samples into the [REDACTION] database. According to management, authorized personnel included floor inspectors and
incoming inspectors. The SOP required the use of forms to authorize addition or deletion of groups, items, samples, and
users to the [REDACTION] system. Forms to be used to authorize the addition or deletion of groups, items, samples, and
users to the [REDACTION] system as specified by the SOP were not used.
c. There was no SOP describing the use of (SP) special samples tested in the Analytical Laboratory. Additionally, special
samples were not listed as a group in the [REDACTION] procedure. Special samples in the testing of Methylphenidate HCl

OBSERVATION 11
Established laboratory control mechanisms are not followed.
a. An Investigation was not issued prior to any retesting for Lot 303087B, Methylphenidate HCl ER 18M stability lot, as required
by procedure SOP # QC­011­03, Laboratory Deviation Investigation. Lot 303087B, Methylphenidate HCl ER Tablets 20 mg,
18M Dissolution stability analysis found that the original L3 testing results were within specification. Two months after the
analysis of 24 tablets for Lot 303087B for 18M stability, 6 more tablets were tested. The results from the final analysis of the 6
tablets were reported as 18 M Dissolution results.
b. SOP # QC­006­01 Retesting and Resampling Analytical Control Laboratory, effective 8/27/03 was not followed for
Methylphenidate HCl ER18M stability lot 303087A:
1. There was no documentation of the number of retests to be performed as required by the SOP. The SOP required the
number of retest to be documented prior to initiating testing to establish a definite limit beyond which no additional testing
would be permitted.
2. The procedure required retests to be conducted by the original chemist and a second chemist, where the second
chemist conducts at least 60% of the tests, or by two chemists, neither of which being the chemist producing the original
result. Retests were not carried out by the original chemist and a second chemist. Additionally, the test was not carried
out by two chemists other than the original chemist.
3. Investigation 04­OOS­031, initiated 12/8/04 and completed 2/18/05, exceeded 30 working days. The procedure required
investigations to be completed in a brief time frame not to exceed 30 working days from the start of the investigation.
Production System
 
OBSERVATION 12
Control procedures are not established which validate the performance of those manufacturing processes that may be
responsible for causing variability in the characteristics of in­process material and the drug product.
a. There is no assurance that results for in­process physical testing are recorded accurately. For example, the Pre­Validation
batch record (TB­110) for Hydrocodone Bitartrate and Acetaminophen Tablets, USP 5mg/325mg shows the specification for
tablet thickness range as 0.308” to 0.358”; this range was crossed out and the correct range of [REDACTION] was
handwritten in the batch record. The in­process tablet thickness results show all tablets were within the corrected thickness
specification of [REDACTION] during compression on 10/15/01. The Research and Development (R&D) In­Process Data
Sheet shows the thickness of 60 tablets to be within a thickness range of 0.330” and 0.334” which corresponds to the tablet
thickness specification which was incorrectly written on the Master Batch Record. Retains from this batch were tested on
6/10/05, and the results show the thickness of the tablets were between [REDACTION] , which was the correct specification
that was handwritten on the Master Batch Record.
b. Manufacturing Investigations into rejected batches of drug products did not include an evaluation of the validated
manufacturing process. For example, seven of nine batches (78%) of Methylphenidate ER 20 mg Tablets, manufactured
between May 2003 and November 2004 were investigated in the laboratory, due to initial OOS results or out of trend results.
Two of the seven lab investigations, resulted in the rejection of batches 411021 and 310004. Manufacturing Investigations,
04­008, for batch 310004, and Manufacturing Investigation 05­001, for batch, 411021 did not include an evaluation of the
validated manufacturing process for Methylphenidate ER 20 mg Tablets.
c. There is no assurance that manufacturing processes for drug products are validated in that out of specification (OOS) results
were generated, but not reported. Several examples are listed below.

For Lot 303087B, Methylphenidate HCl ER 18M stability, an investigation was not issued prior to retesting, and results from an unjustified retest of 6 tablets were reported as the official 18M Dissolution results despite original L3 testing being within specification. evidence_list: An Investigation was not issued prior to any retesting for Lot 303087B, Methylphenidate HCl ER 18M stability lot, as required by procedure SOP # QC-011-03, Laboratory Deviation Investigation.

Lot 303087B, Methylphenidate HCl ER Tablets 20 mg, 18M Dissolution stability analysis found that the original L3 testing results were within specification. Two months after the analysis of 24 tablets for Lot 303087B for 18M stability, 6 more tablets were tested. The results from the final analysis of the 6 tablets were reported as 18 M Dissolution results.
There was no documentation of the number of retests to be performed as required by the SOP.

The procedure required retests to be conducted by the original chemist and a second chemist... Retests were not carried out by the original chemist and a second chemist. Additionally, the test was not carried out by two chemists other than the original chemist.
observations.source_notes_excerpt: Established laboratory control mechanisms are not followed. a. An Investigation was not issued prior to any retesting for Lot 303087B, Methylphenidate HCl ER 18M stability lot, as required by procedure SOP # QC-011-03, Laboratory Deviation Investigation. Lot 303087B, Methylphenidate HCl ER Tablets 20 mg, 18M Dissolution stability analysis found that the original L3 testing results were within specification. Two months after the analysis of 24 tablets for Lot 303087B for 18M stability, 6 more tablets were tested. The results from the final analysis of the 6 tablets were reported as 18 M Dissolution results. b. SOP # QC-006-01 Retesting and Resampling Analytical Control Laboratory, effective 8/27/03 was not followed for Methylphenidate HCl ER18M stability lot 303087A: 1. There was no documentation of the number of retests to be performed as required by the SOP. The SOP required the number of retest to be documented prior to initiating testing to establish a definite limit beyond which no additional testing would be permitted. 2. The procedure required retests to be conducted by the original chemist and a second chemist, where the second chemist conducts at least 60% of the tests, or by two chemists, neither of which being the chemist producing the original result. Retests were not carried out by the original chemist and a second chemist. Additionally, the test was not carried out by two chemists other than the original chemist.
