DURING AN INSPECTION OF YOUR FIRM WE OBSERVED: 
Quality System
OBSERVATION 1

The quality control unit lacks authority to fully investigate errors that have occurred.
The Quality Unit and Senior Management failed to assure all drug products distributed have the safety, identity, quality, and purity
that they are represented to possess. The Quality Unit failed to: review electronic data as part of batch release, review computer
audit trails in the Waters Empower Data Acquisition System and provide adequate training to analytical chemists. These practices
led to the Quality Unit releasing batches of drug products which failed to meet in-process, finished product and stability
specifications. These practices also led to the submission of erroneous data in Annual Reports and Prior Approval Supplement #
004, for ANDA 75-838, which requested discontinuance of Blend Uniformity testing for Propoxyphene Napsylate and
Acetaminophen 100mg/650 mg Tablets. The lack of Quality oversight resulted in: the ceasing of manufacturing on 5/13/05
5/19/05, the ceasing of distribution of all drug products on 5/26/05 5/13/05, the recall of all batches (3,184) of drug products and
the withdrawal of at least five Abbreviated New Drug Applications.

observations.observation_text: Drug products failing to meet established standards, specifications, and quality control criteria are not rejected. The firm routinely re-sampled, re-injected, or reprocessed samples when out-of-specification (OOS) results were obtained, without conducting laboratory investigations or documenting the retesting. Subsequently, within-specification results from these reprocessed samples were reported, leading to the release of drug products with OOS values, such as Acetaminophen & Codeine Phosphate Tablet, Batch 502022, which had an original OOS Blend Uniformity result of 5.4% RSD but was reported as 3.8% RSD.

observations.observation_text:
(1) Annual reports submitted to FDA did not include reports of investigations involving chemical or physical properties that might affect FDA's previous conclusions about the safety or effectiveness of the drug. Specifically, annual reports for ANDAs, such as the one submitted on 8/24/04 for Propoxyphene Napsylate and APAP Tablets, Batch 303110A (ANDA 75-838), only included passing data points and omitted out-of-specification (OOS) results, leading to the submission of erroneous data and subsequent withdrawal of ANDAs. Additionally, a Prior Approval Supplement #004 for ANDA 75-838, submitted on 3/16/04, also contained erroneous data by omitting initial OOS results for Blend Uniformity and Content Uniformity.

(2) The firm failed to submit NDA-Field Alert Reports within three working days of receiving information concerning the failure of distributed drug product batches to meet specifications established in their applications. Specifically, Field Alerts were not filed for multiple batches, including Atenolol 25 mg Tablet, Validation Batch 408107A (ANDA 76-907), which failed dissolution specifications (D5 = 83.7%, D6 = 83.8%) at the 3-month RT stability point, but was reported as passing (D5 = 98.9%, D6 = 98.7%). Additionally, there is no Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) covering the issuance of Field Alerts.

observations.observation_text: Written records of investigations into unexplained discrepancies and the failure of a batch or any of its components to meet specifications are not always made or do not include complete conclusions and follow-up. Laboratory investigations were not conducted when out-of-specification (OOS) results were generated during in-process, finished product, and stability testing, despite the firm's SOP # QC-021-06 requiring such investigations. For example, OOS Investigation # 04-00S-031 for Methylphenidate HCl ER Tablets 20 mg, Lot 303087A, was incomplete, lacking documentation to justify invalidating failing dissolution results and failing to show completion of identified corrective measures or review of data from the same analysts for other lots.

OBSERVATION 7
Written records are not made of investigations into unexplained discrepancies and the failure of a batch or any of its components
to meet specifications.
Laboratory investigations were not conducted when out of specification (OOS) results were generated during in-process, finished
product and stability testing of drug products. Examples of batches where OOS results were generated and not investigated are
included in FDA-483, point # 2. Quality Control Procedure, SOP # QC-021-06, Acceptance/Rejection Criteria for OOS Analytical
Test Results, requires an investigation be conducted when OOS results are generated.
 
OBSERVATION 9
Written records of investigations into unexplained discrepancies and the failure of a batch or any of its components to meet
specifications do not always include the conclusions and followup.
OOS Investigation # 04-00S-031, for Methylphenidate HCl ER Tablets 20 mg 18 month stability lot 303087A was initiated due to
dissolution failing results. The specification required the average of 24 tablets to be within the range of [REDACTION] at the L3, 1
hour dissolution time point. The average of the 24 tablets was reported to be 48.4% with a minimum result of 45.8% and a
maximum of 50.2%. The investigation was found to be incomplete. The investigation concluded that the original failing results
were invalid due to an analyst technique issue. There was no documentation provided within the investigation or within the analyst
notebook to justify invalidating the failing dissolution results. Although corrective measures were identified in the investigation,
there was no documentation to show that the corrective measures had been completed. Additionally, there was no review of data
acquired by the same analysts for the same tests for other lots of the same product.

Furthermore, manufacturing investigations into rejected batches, such as Methylphenidate ER 20 mg Tablets batches 411021 and 310004, did not include an evaluation of the validated manufacturing process. Sheet shows the thickness of 60 tablets to be within a thickness range of 0.330” and 0.334” which corresponds to the tablet
thickness specification which was incorrectly written on the Master Batch Record. Retains from this batch were tested on

observations.observation_text: Laboratory controls do not include scientifically sound and appropriate specifications, standards, sampling plans, and test procedures designed to assure that components, drug product containers, closures, in-process materials, and drug products conform to appropriate standards of identity, strength, quality, and purity. The responsibilities and procedures applicable to the quality control unit are not in writing and fully followed. Specifically, the Laboratory Records SOP # QC-022-04 did not account for large gaps in notebook numbering, and the procedure for notebook issuance was not fully described. SOP Method Number I-037 for sample logging lacked procedures and responsibilities for authorized personnel and required forms for system changes were not used. There was no SOP describing the use of special samples, and special samples were not listed as a group in the [REDACTION] procedure. Additionally, established laboratory control mechanisms were not followed, as an investigation was not issued prior to retesting for Lot 303087B, Methylphenidate HCl ER 18M stability lot, and SOP # QC-006-01 for Retesting and Resampling was not followed for Methylphenidate HCl ER18M stability lot 303087A, lacking documentation of retest numbers and proper chemist involvement.

OBSERVATION 10
The responsibilities and procedures applicable to the quality control unit are not in writing and fully followed.
a. The Laboratory Records SOP # QC-022-04 effective 6/25/04, specified numerically ordered notebooks will be issued and a
log maintained. Notebook issuance logs showed large gaps in numbering of notebooks issued, which were not accounted for
in the log. Additionally, the procedure for issuance of notebooks, as described by management, which indicated a notebook
request form was to be used, was not described in the procedure available.
b. SOP Method Number I-037, approved 10/18/00, General Guidelines for sample Logging for Analytical Laboratory using
[REDACTION] software did not include procedures and responsibilities to be followed by personnel authorized to enter
samples into the [REDACTION] database. According to management, authorized personnel included floor inspectors and
incoming inspectors. The SOP required the use of forms to authorize addition or deletion of groups, items, samples, and
users to the [REDACTION] system. Forms to be used to authorize the addition or deletion of groups, items, samples, and
users to the [REDACTION] system as specified by the SOP were not used.
c. There was no SOP describing the use of (SP) special samples tested in the Analytical Laboratory. Additionally, special
samples were not listed as a group in the [REDACTION] procedure. Special samples in the testing of Methylphenidate HCl

ER Tablets 20mg Lot # 303087A 9MRT SP 04-101 dated 4/24/04(6 tablets) and SP04-101 
(6 tablets) dated 4/26/04 were used to report L3 Dissolution results for the stability sample #ST04-407 for the same lot.
Dissolution testing for L2 and L3 were not labeled L2 and L3 in the notebook.
 
OBSERVATION 11
Established laboratory control mechanisms are not followed.
a. An Investigation was not issued prior to any retesting for Lot 303087B, Methylphenidate HCl ER 18M stability lot, as required
by procedure SOP # QC-011-03, Laboratory Deviation Investigation. Lot 303087B, Methylphenidate HCl ER Tablets 20 mg,
18M Dissolution stability analysis found that the original L3 testing results were within specification. Two months after the
analysis of 24 tablets for Lot 303087B for 18M stability, 6 more tablets were tested. The results from the final analysis of the 6
tablets were reported as 18 M Dissolution results.
b. SOP # QC-006-01 Retesting and Resampling Analytical Control Laboratory, effective 8/27/03 was not followed for
Methylphenidate HCl ER18M stability lot 303087A:
1. There was no documentation of the number of retests to be performed as required by the SOP. The SOP required the
number of retest to be documented prior to initiating testing to establish a definite limit beyond which no additional testing
would be permitted.
2. The procedure required retests to be conducted by the original chemist and a second chemist, where the second
chemist conducts at least 60% of the tests, or by two chemists, neither of which being the chemist producing the original
result. Retests were not carried out by the original chemist and a second chemist. Additionally, the test was not carried
out by two chemists other than the original chemist.
3. Investigation 04-OOS-031, initiated 12/8/04 and completed 2/18/05, exceeded 30 working days. The procedure required
investigations to be completed in a brief time frame not to exceed 30 working days from the start of the investigation.

This document lists observations made by the FDA representative(s) during the inspection of your facility. They are inspectional observations, and do not represent a final
Agency determination regarding your compliance. If you have an objection regarding an observation, or have implemented, or plan to implement, corrective action in
response to an observation, you may discuss the objection or action with the FDA representative(s) during the inspection or submit this information to FDA at the address
above. If you have any questions, please contact FDA at the phone number and address above.
The observations noted in this Form FDA­483 are not an exhaustive listing of objectionable conditions. Under the law, your firm is responsible for conducting internal self­
audits to identify and correct any and all violations of the quality system requirements.
DURING AN INSPECTION OF YOUR FIRM WE OBSERVED: 
Quality System
OBSERVATION 1

6/24/2016

2/12
The quality control unit lacks authority to fully investigate errors that have occurred.
The Quality Unit and Senior Management failed to assure all drug products distributed have the safety, identity, quality, and purity
that they are represented to possess. The Quality Unit failed to: review electronic data as part of batch release, review computer
audit trails in the Waters Empower Data Acquisition System and provide adequate training to analytical chemists. These practices
led to the Quality Unit releasing batches of drug products which failed to meet in­process, finished product and stability
specifications. These practices also led to the submission of erroneous data in Annual Reports and Prior Approval Supplement #
004, for ANDA 75­838, which requested discontinuance of Blend Uniformity testing for Propoxyphene Napsylate and
Acetaminophen 100mg/650 mg Tablets. The lack of Quality oversight resulted in: the ceasing of manufacturing on 5/13/05
5/19/05, the ceasing of distribution of all drug products on 5/26/05 5/13/05, the recall of all batches (3,184) of drug products and
the withdrawal of at least five Abbreviated New Drug Applications.
 
OBSERVATION 2
Drug products failing to meet established standards, specifications, and quality control criteria are not rejected.
Samples of drug products were routinely resampled, and re­injected or reprocessed in the [REDACTION] 
System during testing in the QC Laboratory when out of specification (OOS) results were obtained. There were no Laboratory
Investigations into OOS results or notebook documentation available to explain the re­injection or retesting of in­process, finished
product and stability samples which did not meet specifications. The OOS results were not reported and within specification
results from reprocessed or re­injected samples were reported on: In­Process Specification, Product Specification and Stability
Study Specification Release Reports and Stability Summary Reports.

OBSERVATION 7
Written records are not made of investigations into unexplained discrepancies and the failure of a batch or any of its components
to meet specifications.
Laboratory investigations were not conducted when out of specification (OOS) results were generated during in­process, finished
product and stability testing of drug products. Examples of batches where OOS results were generated and not investigated are
included in FDA­483, point # 2. Quality Control Procedure, SOP # QC­021­06, Acceptance/Rejection Criteria for OOS Analytical
Test Results, requires an investigation be conducted when OOS results are generated.
 
OBSERVATION 8
Employees are not given training in current good manufacturing practices and written procedures required by current good
manufacturing practice regulations.
QC Laboratory analysts were not routinely trained in Quality Control procedures such as SOP # QC­011­03, Laboratory Deviation
Investigations and SOP # QC­021­06, Acceptance/Rejection Criteria for OOS Analytical Test Results. This lack of training and
oversight by management contributed to the non­reporting of OOS results in the QC Laboratory.
 
OBSERVATION 9
Written records of investigations into unexplained discrepancies and the failure of a batch or any of its components to meet
specifications do not always include the conclusions and followup.
OOS Investigation # 04­00S­031, for Methylphenidate HCl ER Tablets 20 mg 18 month stability lot 303087A was initiated due to
dissolution failing results. The specification required the average of 24 tablets to be within the range of [REDACTION] at the L3, 1
hour dissolution time point. The average of the 24 tablets was reported to be 48.4% with a minimum result of 45.8% and a
maximum of 50.2%. The investigation was found to be incomplete. The investigation concluded that the original failing results
were invalid due to an analyst technique issue. There was no documentation provided within the investigation or within the analyst
notebook to justify invalidating the failing dissolution results. Although corrective measures were identified in the investigation,
there was no documentation to show that the corrective measures had been completed. Additionally, there was no review of data
acquired by the same analysts for the same tests for other lots of the same product.

OBSERVATION 11
Established laboratory control mechanisms are not followed.
a. An Investigation was not issued prior to any retesting for Lot 303087B, Methylphenidate HCl ER 18M stability lot, as required
by procedure SOP # QC­011­03, Laboratory Deviation Investigation. Lot 303087B, Methylphenidate HCl ER Tablets 20 mg,
18M Dissolution stability analysis found that the original L3 testing results were within specification. Two months after the
analysis of 24 tablets for Lot 303087B for 18M stability, 6 more tablets were tested. The results from the final analysis of the 6
tablets were reported as 18 M Dissolution results.
b. SOP # QC­006­01 Retesting and Resampling Analytical Control Laboratory, effective 8/27/03 was not followed for
Methylphenidate HCl ER18M stability lot 303087A:
1. There was no documentation of the number of retests to be performed as required by the SOP. The SOP required the
number of retest to be documented prior to initiating testing to establish a definite limit beyond which no additional testing
would be permitted.
2. The procedure required retests to be conducted by the original chemist and a second chemist, where the second
chemist conducts at least 60% of the tests, or by two chemists, neither of which being the chemist producing the original
result. Retests were not carried out by the original chemist and a second chemist. Additionally, the test was not carried
out by two chemists other than the original chemist.
3. Investigation 04­OOS­031, initiated 12/8/04 and completed 2/18/05, exceeded 30 working days. The procedure required
investigations to be completed in a brief time frame not to exceed 30 working days from the start of the investigation.

OBSERVATION 12
Control procedures are not established which validate the performance of those manufacturing processes that may be
responsible for causing variability in the characteristics of in­process material and the drug product.
a. There is no assurance that results for in­process physical testing are recorded accurately. For example, the Pre­Validation
batch record (TB­110) for Hydrocodone Bitartrate and Acetaminophen Tablets, USP 5mg/325mg shows the specification for
tablet thickness range as 0.308” to 0.358”; this range was crossed out and the correct range of [REDACTION] was
handwritten in the batch record. The in­process tablet thickness results show all tablets were within the corrected thickness
specification of [REDACTION] during compression on 10/15/01. The Research and Development (R&D) In­Process Data
Sheet shows the thickness of 60 tablets to be within a thickness range of 0.330” and 0.334” which corresponds to the tablet
thickness specification which was incorrectly written on the Master Batch Record. Retains from this batch were tested on
6/10/05, and the results show the thickness of the tablets were between [REDACTION] , which was the correct specification
that was handwritten on the Master Batch Record.
b. Manufacturing Investigations into rejected batches of drug products did not include an evaluation of the validated
manufacturing process. For example, seven of nine batches (78%) of Methylphenidate ER 20 mg Tablets, manufactured
between May 2003 and November 2004 were investigated in the laboratory, due to initial OOS results or out of trend results.
Two of the seven lab investigations, resulted in the rejection of batches 411021 and 310004. Manufacturing Investigations,
04­008, for batch 310004, and Manufacturing Investigation 05­001, for batch, 411021 did not include an evaluation of the
validated manufacturing process for Methylphenidate ER 20 mg Tablets.
c. There is no assurance that manufacturing processes for drug products are validated in that out of specification (OOS) results

    "observation_text": "The quality control unit lacks the authority to fully investigate errors and fails to assure that all drug products distributed possess the required safety, identity, quality, and purity.",
    "cfr_citation": "21 CFR 211.22(a)",
    "evidence_list": [
      "The quality control unit lacks authority to fully investigate errors that have occurred.",
      "The Quality Unit and Senior Management failed to assure all drug products distributed have the safety, identity, quality, and purity that they are represented to possess."

    "source_notes_excerpt": "OBSERVATION 1
The quality control unit lacks authority to fully investigate errors that have occurred.
The Quality Unit and Senior Management failed to assure all drug products distributed have the safety, identity, quality, and purity
that they are represented to possess. The Quality Unit failed to: review electronic data as part of batch release, review computer
audit trails in the Waters Empower Data Acquisition System and provide adequate training to analytical chemists. These practices
led to the Quality Unit releasing batches of drug products which failed to meet in-process, finished product and stability
specifications. These practices also led to the submission of erroneous data in Annual Reports and Prior Approval Supplement #
004, for ANDA 75-838, which requested discontinuance of Blend Uniformity testing for Propoxyphene Napsylate and
Acetaminophen 100mg/650 mg Tablets. The lack of Quality oversight resulted in: the ceasing of manufacturing on 5/13/05
5/19/05, the ceasing of distribution of all drug products on 5/26/05 5/13/05, the recall of all batches (3,184) of drug products and
the withdrawal of at least five Abbreviated New Drug Applications."

    "source_notes_excerpt": "There were no Laboratory Investigations into OOS results or notebook documentation available to explain the re-injection or retesting of in-process, finished product and stability samples which did not meet specifications. ... OBSERVATION 7 Written records are not made of investigations into unexplained discrepancies and the failure of a batch or any of its components to meet specifications. Laboratory investigations were not conducted when out of specification (OOS) results were generated during in-process, finished product and stability testing of drug products. Examples of batches where OOS results were generated and not investigated are included in FDA-483, point # 2. Quality Control Procedure, SOP # QC-021-06, Acceptance/Rejection Criteria for OOS Analytical Test Results, requires an investigation be conducted when OOS results are generated. ... OBSERVATION 9 Written records of investigations into unexplained discrepancies and the failure of a batch or any of its components to meet specifications do not always include the conclusions and followup. OOS Investigation # 04-00S-031, for Methylphenidate HCl ER Tablets 20 mg 18 month stability lot 303087A was initiated due to dissolution failing results. The specification required the average of 24 tablets to be within the range of [REDACTION] at the L3, 1 hour dissolution time point. The average of the 24 tablets was reported to be 48.4% with a minimum result of 45.8% and a maximum of 50.2%. The investigation was found to be incomplete. The investigation concluded that the original failing results were invalid due to an analyst technique issue. There was no documentation provided within the investigation or within the analyst notebook to justify invalidating the failing dissolution results. Although corrective measures were identified in the investigation, there was no documentation to show that the corrective measures had been completed. Additionally, there was no review of data acquired by the same analysts for the same tests for other lots of the same product. ... Manufacturing Investigations into rejected batches of drug products did not include an evaluation of the validated manufacturing process. For example, seven of nine batches (78%) of Methylphenidate ER 20 mg Tablets, manufactured between May 2003 and November 2004 were investigated in the laboratory, due to initial OOS results or out of trend results. Two of the seven lab investigations, resulted in the rejection of batches 411021 and 310004. Written records of investigations into unexplained discrepancies and the failure of a batch or any of its components to meet
specifications do not always include the conclusions and followup.
OOS Investigation # 04-00S-031, for Methylphenidate HCl ER Tablets 20 mg 18 month stability lot 303087A was initiated due to
dissolution failing results. The specification required the average of 24 tablets to be within the range of [REDACTION] at the L3, 1
hour dissolution time point. The average of the 24 tablets was reported to be 48.4% with a minimum result of 45.8% and a
maximum of 50.2%. The investigation was found to be incomplete. The investigation concluded that the original failing results
were invalid due to an analyst technique issue. There was no documentation provided within the investigation or within the analyst
notebook to justify invalidating the failing dissolution results. Although corrective measures were identified in the investigation,
there was no documentation to show that the corrective measures had been completed. Additionally, there was no review of data
acquired by the same analysts for the same tests for other lots of the same product.

2/12
The quality control unit lacks authority to fully investigate errors that have occurred.
The Quality Unit and Senior Management failed to assure all drug products distributed have the safety, identity, quality, and purity
that they are represented to possess. The Quality Unit failed to: review electronic data as part of batch release, review computer
audit trails in the Waters Empower Data Acquisition System and provide adequate training to analytical chemists. These practices
led to the Quality Unit releasing batches of drug products which failed to meet in­process, finished product and stability
specifications. These practices also led to the submission of erroneous data in Annual Reports and Prior Approval Supplement #
004, for ANDA 75­838, which requested discontinuance of Blend Uniformity testing for Propoxyphene Napsylate and
Acetaminophen 100mg/650 mg Tablets. The lack of Quality oversight resulted in: the ceasing of manufacturing on 5/13/05
5/19/05, the ceasing of distribution of all drug products on 5/26/05 5/13/05, the recall of all batches (3,184) of drug products and
the withdrawal of at least five Abbreviated New Drug Applications.
 
OBSERVATION 2
Drug products failing to meet established standards, specifications, and quality control criteria are not rejected.
Samples of drug products were routinely resampled, and re­injected or reprocessed in the [REDACTION] 
System during testing in the QC Laboratory when out of specification (OOS) results were obtained. There were no Laboratory
Investigations into OOS results or notebook documentation available to explain the re­injection or retesting of in­process, finished
product and stability samples which did not meet specifications. The OOS results were not reported and within specification
results from reprocessed or re­injected samples were reported on: In­Process Specification, Product Specification and Stability
Study Specification Release Reports and Stability Summary Reports.

observations.observation_text: The Quality Control Unit lacks the authority and responsibility to fully investigate errors, assure the quality of drug products, and adequately review electronic data and computer audit trails, leading to the release of non-conforming products and the submission of erroneous data to the Agency.

evidence_list: The quality control unit lacks authority to fully investigate errors that have occurred.
The Quality Unit and Senior Management failed to assure all drug products distributed have the safety, identity, quality, and purity that they are represented to possess.

The Quality Unit failed to: review electronic data as part of batch release, review computer audit trails in the Waters Empower Data Acquisition System and provide adequate training to analytical chemists.
These practices led to the Quality Unit releasing batches of drug products which failed to meet in-process, finished product and stability specifications.

These practices also led to the submission of erroneous data in Annual Reports and Prior Approval Supplement # 004, for ANDA 75-838, which requested discontinuance of Blend Uniformity testing for Propoxyphene Napsylate and Acetaminophen 100mg/650 mg Tablets.

The lack of Quality oversight resulted in: the ceasing of manufacturing on 5/13/05 5/19/05, the ceasing of distribution of all drug products on 5/26/05 5/13/05, the recall of all batches (3,184) of drug products and the withdrawal of at least five Abbreviated New Drug Applications.

(1) Annual reports submitted to FDA did not include out-of-specification (OOS) results, only passing data points, and a Prior Approval Supplement contained erroneous data, which affected FDA's conclusions about the safety or effectiveness of the drug.

(2) Field Alert Reports were not submitted within three working days of receipt of information concerning the failure of distributed batches of drug products to meet specifications, and there is no Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) covering the issuance of Field Alerts.

evidence_list: Written records are not made of investigations into unexplained discrepancies and the failure of a batch or any of its components to meet specifications.
Laboratory investigations were not conducted when out of specification (OOS) results were generated during in-process, finished product and stability testing of drug products.
Examples of batches where OOS results were generated and not investigated are included in FDA-483, point # 2.
Quality Control Procedure, SOP # QC-021-06, Acceptance/Rejection Criteria for OOS Analytical Test Results, requires an investigation be conducted when OOS results are generated.
OOS Investigation # 04-00S-031, for Methylphenidate HCl ER Tablets 20 mg 18 month stability lot 303087A was initiated due to dissolution failing results. The investigation was found to be incomplete.

The investigation concluded that the original failing results were invalid due to an analyst technique issue. There was no documentation provided within the investigation or within the analyst notebook to justify invalidating the failing dissolution results.
Although corrective measures were identified in the investigation, there was no documentation to show that the corrective measures had been completed.
Additionally, there was no review of data acquired by the same analysts for the same tests for other lots of the same product.

Written records are not made of investigations into unexplained discrepancies and the failure of a batch or any of its components
to meet specifications.
Laboratory investigations were not conducted when out of specification (OOS) results were generated during in-process, finished
product and stability testing of drug products. Examples of batches where OOS results were generated and not investigated are
included in FDA-483, point # 2. Quality Control Procedure, SOP # QC-021-06, Acceptance/Rejection Criteria for OOS Analytical
Test Results, requires an investigation be conducted when OOS results are generated.
 
OBSERVATION 8
Employees are not given training in current good manufacturing practices and written procedures required by current good
manufacturing practice regulations.
QC Laboratory analysts were not routinely trained in Quality Control procedures such as SOP # QC-011-03, Laboratory Deviation
Investigations and SOP # QC-021-06, Acceptance/Rejection Criteria for OOS Analytical Test Results. This lack of training and
oversight by management contributed to the non-reporting of OOS results in the QC Laboratory.
 
OBSERVATION 9
Written records of investigations into unexplained discrepancies and the failure of a batch or any of its components to meet
specifications do not always include the conclusions and followup.
OOS Investigation # 04-00S-031, for Methylphenidate HCl ER Tablets 20 mg 18 month stability lot 303087A was initiated due to
dissolution failing results. The specification required the average of 24 tablets to be within the range of [REDACTION] at the L3, 1
hour dissolution time point. The average of the 24 tablets was reported to be 48.4% with a minimum result of 45.8% and a
maximum of 50.2%. The investigation was found to be incomplete. The investigation concluded that the original failing results
were invalid due to an analyst technique issue. There was no documentation provided within the investigation or within the analyst
notebook to justify invalidating the failing dissolution results. Although corrective measures were identified in the investigation,
there was no documentation to show that the corrective measures had been completed. Additionally, there was no review of data
acquired by the same analysts for the same tests for other lots of the same product.

OBSERVATION 11
Established laboratory control mechanisms are not followed.
a. An Investigation was not issued prior to any retesting for Lot 303087B, Methylphenidate HCl ER 18M stability lot, as required
by procedure SOP # QC-011-03, Laboratory Deviation Investigation. Lot 303087B, Methylphenidate HCl ER Tablets 20 mg,
18M Dissolution stability analysis found that the original L3 testing results were within specification. Two months after the
analysis of 24 tablets for Lot 303087B for 18M stability, 6 more tablets were tested. The results from the final analysis of the 6
tablets were reported as 18 M Dissolution results.
b. SOP # QC-006-01 Retesting and Resampling Analytical Control Laboratory, effective 8/27/03 was not followed for
Methylphenidate HCl ER18M stability lot 303087A:
1. There was no documentation of the number of retests to be performed as required by the SOP. The SOP required the
number of retest to be documented prior to initiating testing to establish a definite limit beyond which no additional testing
would be permitted.
2. The procedure required retests to be conducted by the original chemist and a second chemist, where the second
chemist conducts at least 60% of the tests, or by two chemists, neither of which being the chemist producing the original
result. Retests were not carried out by the original chemist and a second chemist. Additionally, the test was not carried
out by two chemists other than the original chemist.
3. Investigation 04-OOS-031, initiated 12/8/04 and completed 2/18/05, exceeded 30 working days. The procedure required
investigations to be completed in a brief time frame not to exceed 30 working days from the start of the investigation.
Production System
 
OBSERVATION 12
Control procedures are not established which validate the performance of those manufacturing processes that may be
responsible for causing variability in the characteristics of in-process material and the drug product.
a. There is no assurance that results for in-process physical testing are recorded accurately. For example, the Pre-Validation
batch record (TB-110) for Hydrocodone Bitartrate and Acetaminophen Tablets, USP 5mg/325mg shows the specification for
tablet thickness range as 0.308” to 0.358”; this range was crossed out and the correct range of [REDACTION] was
handwritten in the batch record. The in-process tablet thickness results show all tablets were within the corrected thickness
specification of [REDACTION] during compression on 10/15/01. The Research and Development (R&D) In-Process Data
Sheet shows the thickness of 60 tablets to be within a thickness range of 0.330” and 0.334” which corresponds to the tablet
thickness specification which was incorrectly written on the Master Batch Record. Retains from this batch were tested on
6/10/05, and the results show the thickness of the tablets were between [REDACTION] , which was the correct specification
that was handwritten on the Master Batch Record.
b. Manufacturing Investigations into rejected batches of drug products did not include an evaluation of the validated
manufacturing process. For example, seven of nine batches (78%) of Methylphenidate ER 20 mg Tablets, manufactured
between May 2003 and November 2004 were investigated in the laboratory, due to initial OOS results or out of trend results.
Two of the seven lab investigations, resulted in the rejection of batches 411021 and 310004. Manufacturing Investigations,
04-008, for batch 310004, and Manufacturing Investigation 05-001, for batch, 411021 did not include an evaluation of the
validated manufacturing process for Methylphenidate ER 20 mg Tablets.
c. There is no assurance that manufacturing processes for drug products are validated in that out of specification (OOS) results

that they are represented to possess. The Quality Unit failed to: review electronic data as part of batch release, review computer
audit trails in the Waters Empower Data Acquisition System and provide adequate training to analytical chemists. These practices
led to the Quality Unit releasing batches of drug products which failed to meet in­process, finished product and stability
specifications. These practices also led to the submission of erroneous data in Annual Reports and Prior Approval Supplement #
004, for ANDA 75­838, which requested discontinuance of Blend Uniformity testing for Propoxyphene Napsylate and
Acetaminophen 100mg/650 mg Tablets. The lack of Quality oversight resulted in: the ceasing of manufacturing on 5/13/05
5/19/05, the ceasing of distribution of all drug products on 5/26/05 5/13/05, the recall of all batches (3,184) of drug products and
the withdrawal of at least five Abbreviated New Drug Applications.
 
OBSERVATION 2
Drug products failing to meet established standards, specifications, and quality control criteria are not rejected.
Samples of drug products were routinely resampled, and re­injected or reprocessed in the [REDACTION] 
System during testing in the QC Laboratory when out of specification (OOS) results were obtained. There were no Laboratory
Investigations into OOS results or notebook documentation available to explain the re­injection or retesting of in­process, finished
product and stability samples which did not meet specifications. The OOS results were not reported and within specification
results from reprocessed or re­injected samples were reported on: In­Process Specification, Product Specification and Stability
Study Specification Release Reports and Stability Summary Reports.

dissolution failing results. The specification required the average of 24 tablets to be within the range of [REDACTION] at the L3, 1
hour dissolution time point. The average of the 24 tablets was reported to be 48.4% with a minimum result of 45.8% and a

observations.observation_text: The quality control unit lacks authority to fully investigate errors that have occurred. The Quality Unit and Senior Management failed to assure all drug products distributed have the safety, identity, quality, and purity that they are represented to possess. The Quality Unit failed to: review electronic data as part of batch release, review computer audit trails in the Waters Empower Data Acquisition System and provide adequate training to analytical chemists. These practices led to the Quality Unit releasing batches of drug products which failed to meet in-process, finished product and stability specifications. These practices also led to the submission of erroneous data in Annual Reports and Prior Approval Supplement # 004, for ANDA 75-838, which requested discontinuance of Blend Uniformity testing for Propoxyphene Napsylate and Acetaminophen 100mg/650 mg Tablets. The lack of Quality oversight resulted in: the ceasing of manufacturing on 5/13/05 5/19/05, the ceasing of distribution of all drug products on 5/26/05 5/13/05, the recall of all batches (3,184) of drug products and the withdrawal of at least five Abbreviated New Drug Applications.

observations.observation_text: Drug products failing to meet established standards, specifications, and quality control criteria are not rejected. Samples of drug products were routinely resampled, and re-injected or reprocessed in the [REDACTION] System during testing in the QC Laboratory when out of specification (OOS) results were obtained. There were no Laboratory Investigations into OOS results or notebook documentation available to explain the re-injection or retesting of in-process, finished product and stability samples which did not meet specifications. The OOS results were not reported and within specification results from reprocessed or re-injected samples were reported on: In-Process Specification, Product Specification and Stability Study Specification Release Reports and Stability Summary Reports. Examples of drug products released with OOS values include Acetaminophen & Codeine Phosphate Tablet, Atenolol Tablet, Bethanechol Chloride Tablet, Diphenoxylate HCl and Atropine Sulfate Tablets, Dytan Suspension, Methylphenidate HCl Tablets, Nitroglycerin Sublingual Tablets, Prochlorperazine Suppositories, and Propoxyphene Napsylate and APAP Tablets.

observations.observation_text: An NDA-Field Alert Report was not submitted within three working days of receipt of information concerning a failure of one or more distributed batches of a drug to meet the specifications established for it in the application. Field Alerts were not routinely filed when drug products did not meet the specifications listed in the Abbreviated New Drug Application (ANDA). There is no SOP covering the issuance of Field Alerts. For example, Field Alerts were not submitted when Atenolol 25 mg Tablet Validation Batch 408107A (ANDA 76-907) failed dissolution specifications at 3 months RT (D5 = 83.7%, D6 = 83.8%), when Atenolol 25 mg Tablet Validation Batch 408107B (ANDA 76-907) failed dissolution specifications at 3 months RT (D6 = 30.9%), when Diphenoxylate HCl and Atropine Sulfate Tablet, Batch 301068A (ANDA 40-395) failed assay specifications for Atropine at 21 months RT (A1 = 78.4%, A2 = 78.7%), when Propoxyphene Napsylate and APAP Tablets, 100/650mg Batch 303110A (ANDA 75-838) failed dissolution specifications at 12 months RT (D1 = 72.8%, D5 = 73.2%), when Propoxyphene Napsylate and APAP Tablets, 100/650mg Batch 104026B Validation Batch (ANDA 75-838) failed assay specifications for Propoxyphene at 6 months RT (A2 = 89.9%), when Propoxyphene Napsylate and APAP Tablets, 100/650mg Batch 201016C (ANDA 75-838) failed assay specifications for Propoxyphene (A1 = 89.9%) and APAP (A1 = 88.7%) at 24 months RT, when Prochlorperazine Suppositories, 2.5 mg Batch 308029A (ANDA 40-407) failed unknown impurities specifications at Initial (0.41%, 0.37%), 6M (0.28%, 0.29%, 0.23%), 9M (0.32%, 0.33%), and 12M (0.52%, 0.73%) RT, and when Prochlorperazine Suppositories, 5 mg Batch 308030A (ANDA 40-407) failed unknown impurities specifications at 3M (0.32%), 6M (0.30%), and 12M (0.44%, 0.56%) RT.

observations.observation_text: Laboratory records do not include complete data derived from all tests, examinations and assay necessary to assure compliance with established specifications and standards. The QC Laboratory notebooks and binders lacked data from all analytical testing conducted in the QC Laboratory. Laboratory records did not include all data such as out of specification (OOS) results, chromatograms, sample weights, and processing methods. OOS results were substituted with passing results by Analysts and Supervisors. The substitution of data was performed by cutting and pasting of chromatograms, substituting vials, changing sample weights and changing processing methods. For products and batches listed in FDA-483, point # 2, OOS results were not documented in laboratory records, but found in electronic data files. For Propoxyphene Napsylate and APAP Tablets, 100/650mg Batch 303110A, chromatogram headers were changed by cutting and pasting for Dissolution Testing of Tablets D1 and D5. For Propoxyphene Napsylate and APAP Tablets, 100/650mg Batch 104026B Validation Batch, original sample weights were not recorded in the notebook; sample weights were changed by the analyst until a passing result was obtained for Assay (A2). For Acetaminophen & Codeine Phosphate Tablets, 300/30mg Batch 407148, processing methods were changed by the analyst until a passing result was obtained, and the original processing method was not recorded in the laboratory notebook.

For example, OOS Investigation # 04-00S-031, for Methylphenidate HCl ER Tablets 20 mg 18 month stability lot 303087A, was initiated due to dissolution failing results (average of 24 tablets reported as 48.4% vs. specification range of [REDACTION]). Additionally, there was no review of data acquired by the same analysts for the same tests for other lots of the same product.

a. The Laboratory Records SOP # QC-022-04 effective 6/25/04, specified numerically ordered notebooks will be issued and a log maintained. b. According to management, authorized personnel included floor inspectors and incoming inspectors. The SOP required the use of forms to authorize addition or deletion of groups, items, samples, and users to the [REDACTION] system. Forms to be used to authorize the addition or deletion of groups, items, samples, and users to the [REDACTION] system as specified by the SOP were not used.
c. There was no SOP describing the use of (SP) special samples tested in the Analytical Laboratory. Additionally, special samples were not listed as a group in the [REDACTION] procedure. Special samples in the testing of Methylphenidate HCl ER Tablets 20mg Lot # 303087A 9MRT SP 04-101 dated 4/24/04(6 tablets) and SP04-101 (6 tablets) dated 4/26/04 were used to report L3 Dissolution results for the stability sample #ST04-407 for the same lot. Dissolution testing for L2 and L3 were not labeled L2 and L3 in the notebook.

observations.source_notes_excerpt:
Established laboratory control mechanisms are not followed.
a. An Investigation was not issued prior to any retesting for Lot 303087B, Methylphenidate HCl ER 18M stability lot, as required by procedure SOP # QC-011-03, Laboratory Deviation Investigation. Lot 303087B, Methylphenidate HCl ER Tablets 20 mg, 18M Dissolution stability analysis found that the original L3 testing results were within specification. Two months after the analysis of 24 tablets for Lot 303087B for 18M stability, 6 more tablets were tested. The results from the final analysis of the 6 tablets were reported as 18 M Dissolution results.
b. SOP # QC-006-01 Retesting and Resampling Analytical Control Laboratory, effective 8/27/03 was not followed for Methylphenidate HCl ER18M stability lot 303087A:
1. There was no documentation of the number of retests to be performed as required by the SOP. The SOP required the number of retest to be documented prior to initiating testing to establish a definite limit beyond which no additional testing would be permitted.
2. The procedure required retests to be conducted by the original chemist and a second chemist, where the second chemist conducts at least 60% of the tests, or by two chemists, neither of which being the chemist producing the original result. Retests were not carried out by the original chemist and a second chemist. Additionally, the test was not carried out by two chemists other than the original chemist.
3. Investigation 04-OOS-031, initiated 12/8/04 and completed 2/18/05, exceeded 30 working days. The procedure required investigations to be completed in a brief time frame not to exceed 30 working days from the start of the investigation.

Control procedures are not established which validate the performance of those manufacturing processes that may be responsible for causing variability in the characteristics of in-process material and the drug product.
a. There is no assurance that results for in-process physical testing are recorded accurately. For example, the Pre-Validation batch record (TB-110) for Hydrocodone Bitartrate and Acetaminophen Tablets, USP 5mg/325mg shows the specification for tablet thickness range as 0.308” to 0.358”; this range was crossed out and the correct range of [REDACTION] was handwritten in the batch record. The in-process tablet thickness results show all tablets were within the corrected thickness specification of [REDACTION] during compression on 10/15/01. The Research and Development (R&D) In-Process Data Sheet shows the thickness of 60 tablets to be within a thickness range of 0.330” and 0.334” which corresponds to the tablet thickness specification which was incorrectly written on the Master Batch Record. Retains from this batch were tested on 6/10/05, and the results show the thickness of the tablets were between [REDACTION] , which was the correct specification that was handwritten on the Master Batch Record.
b. Manufacturing Investigations into rejected batches of drug products did not include an evaluation of the validated manufacturing process. For example, seven of nine batches (78%) of Methylphenidate ER 20 mg Tablets, manufactured between May 2003 and November 2004 were investigated in the laboratory, due to initial OOS results or out of trend results. Two of the seven lab investigations, resulted in the rejection of batches 411021 and 310004. Manufacturing Investigations, 04-008, for batch 310004, and Manufacturing Investigation 05-001, for batch, 411021 did not include an evaluation of the validated manufacturing process for Methylphenidate ER 20 mg Tablets.

Quality System
OBSERVATION 1

6/24/2016

2/12
The quality control unit lacks authority to fully investigate errors that have occurred.
The Quality Unit and Senior Management failed to assure all drug products distributed have the safety, identity, quality, and purity
that they are represented to possess. The Quality Unit failed to: review electronic data as part of batch release, review computer
audit trails in the Waters Empower Data Acquisition System and provide adequate training to analytical chemists. These practices
led to the Quality Unit releasing batches of drug products which failed to meet in­process, finished product and stability
specifications. These practices also led to the submission of erroneous data in Annual Reports and Prior Approval Supplement #
004, for ANDA 75­838, which requested discontinuance of Blend Uniformity testing for Propoxyphene Napsylate and
Acetaminophen 100mg/650 mg Tablets. The lack of Quality oversight resulted in: the ceasing of manufacturing on 5/13/05
5/19/05, the ceasing of distribution of all drug products on 5/26/05 5/13/05, the recall of all batches (3,184) of drug products and
the withdrawal of at least five Abbreviated New Drug Applications.
 
OBSERVATION 2
Drug products failing to meet established standards, specifications, and quality control criteria are not rejected.
Samples of drug products were routinely resampled, and re­injected or reprocessed in the [REDACTION] 
System during testing in the QC Laboratory when out of specification (OOS) results were obtained. There were no Laboratory
Investigations into OOS results or notebook documentation available to explain the re­injection or retesting of in­process, finished
product and stability samples which did not meet specifications. The OOS results were not reported and within specification
results from reprocessed or re­injected samples were reported on: In­Process Specification, Product Specification and Stability
Study Specification Release Reports and Stability Summary Reports.

OBSERVATION 7
Written records are not made of investigations into unexplained discrepancies and the failure of a batch or any of its components
to meet specifications.
Laboratory investigations were not conducted when out of specification (OOS) results were generated during in­process, finished
product and stability testing of drug products. Examples of batches where OOS results were generated and not investigated are
included in FDA­483, point # 2. Quality Control Procedure, SOP # QC­021­06, Acceptance/Rejection Criteria for OOS Analytical
Test Results, requires an investigation be conducted when OOS results are generated.
 
OBSERVATION 8
Employees are not given training in current good manufacturing practices and written procedures required by current good
manufacturing practice regulations.
QC Laboratory analysts were not routinely trained in Quality Control procedures such as SOP # QC­011­03, Laboratory Deviation
Investigations and SOP # QC­021­06, Acceptance/Rejection Criteria for OOS Analytical Test Results. This lack of training and
oversight by management contributed to the non­reporting of OOS results in the QC Laboratory.
 
OBSERVATION 9
Written records of investigations into unexplained discrepancies and the failure of a batch or any of its components to meet
specifications do not always include the conclusions and followup.
OOS Investigation # 04­00S­031, for Methylphenidate HCl ER Tablets 20 mg 18 month stability lot 303087A was initiated due to
dissolution failing results. The specification required the average of 24 tablets to be within the range of [REDACTION] at the L3, 1
hour dissolution time point. The average of the 24 tablets was reported to be 48.4% with a minimum result of 45.8% and a
maximum of 50.2%. The investigation was found to be incomplete. The investigation concluded that the original failing results
were invalid due to an analyst technique issue. There was no documentation provided within the investigation or within the analyst
notebook to justify invalidating the failing dissolution results. Although corrective measures were identified in the investigation,
there was no documentation to show that the corrective measures had been completed. Additionally, there was no review of data
acquired by the same analysts for the same tests for other lots of the same product.

OBSERVATION 11
Established laboratory control mechanisms are not followed.
a. An Investigation was not issued prior to any retesting for Lot 303087B, Methylphenidate HCl ER 18M stability lot, as required
by procedure SOP # QC­011­03, Laboratory Deviation Investigation. Lot 303087B, Methylphenidate HCl ER Tablets 20 mg,
18M Dissolution stability analysis found that the original L3 testing results were within specification. Two months after the
analysis of 24 tablets for Lot 303087B for 18M stability, 6 more tablets were tested. The results from the final analysis of the 6
tablets were reported as 18 M Dissolution results.
b. SOP # QC­006­01 Retesting and Resampling Analytical Control Laboratory, effective 8/27/03 was not followed for
Methylphenidate HCl ER18M stability lot 303087A:
1. There was no documentation of the number of retests to be performed as required by the SOP. The SOP required the
number of retest to be documented prior to initiating testing to establish a definite limit beyond which no additional testing
would be permitted.
2. The procedure required retests to be conducted by the original chemist and a second chemist, where the second
chemist conducts at least 60% of the tests, or by two chemists, neither of which being the chemist producing the original
result. Retests were not carried out by the original chemist and a second chemist. Additionally, the test was not carried
out by two chemists other than the original chemist.
3. Investigation 04­OOS­031, initiated 12/8/04 and completed 2/18/05, exceeded 30 working days. The procedure required
investigations to be completed in a brief time frame not to exceed 30 working days from the start of the investigation.

OBSERVATION 12
Control procedures are not established which validate the performance of those manufacturing processes that may be
responsible for causing variability in the characteristics of in­process material and the drug product.
a. There is no assurance that results for in­process physical testing are recorded accurately. For example, the Pre­Validation
batch record (TB­110) for Hydrocodone Bitartrate and Acetaminophen Tablets, USP 5mg/325mg shows the specification for
tablet thickness range as 0.308” to 0.358”; this range was crossed out and the correct range of [REDACTION] was
handwritten in the batch record. The in­process tablet thickness results show all tablets were within the corrected thickness
specification of [REDACTION] during compression on 10/15/01. The Research and Development (R&D) In­Process Data
Sheet shows the thickness of 60 tablets to be within a thickness range of 0.330” and 0.334” which corresponds to the tablet
thickness specification which was incorrectly written on the Master Batch Record. Retains from this batch were tested on
6/10/05, and the results show the thickness of the tablets were between [REDACTION] , which was the correct specification
that was handwritten on the Master Batch Record.
b. Manufacturing Investigations into rejected batches of drug products did not include an evaluation of the validated
manufacturing process. For example, seven of nine batches (78%) of Methylphenidate ER 20 mg Tablets, manufactured
between May 2003 and November 2004 were investigated in the laboratory, due to initial OOS results or out of trend results.
Two of the seven lab investigations, resulted in the rejection of batches 411021 and 310004. Manufacturing Investigations,
04­008, for batch 310004, and Manufacturing Investigation 05­001, for batch, 411021 did not include an evaluation of the
validated manufacturing process for Methylphenidate ER 20 mg Tablets.
c. There is no assurance that manufacturing processes for drug products are validated in that out of specification (OOS) results

observations.observation_text: The quality control unit lacks authority to fully investigate errors that have occurred. The Quality Unit and Senior Management failed to assure all drug products distributed have the safety, identity, quality, and purity that they are represented to possess. The Quality Unit failed to: review electronic data as part of batch release, review computer audit trails in the Waters Empower Data Acquisition System and provide adequate training to analytical chemists. These practices led to the Quality Unit releasing batches of drug products which failed to meet in-process, finished product and stability specifications. These practices also led to the submission of erroneous data in Annual Reports and Prior Approval Supplement # 004, for ANDA 75-838, which requested discontinuance of Blend Uniformity testing for Propoxyphene Napsylate and Acetaminophen 100mg/650 mg Tablets. The lack of Quality oversight resulted in: the ceasing of manufacturing on 5/13/05 5/19/05, the ceasing of distribution of all drug products on 5/26/05 5/13/05, the recall of all batches (3,184) of drug products and the withdrawal of at least five Abbreviated New Drug Applications.

Drug products failing to meet established standards, specifications, and quality control criteria are not rejected. Samples of drug products were routinely resampled, and re-injected or reprocessed in the [REDACTION] System during testing in the QC Laboratory when out of specification (OOS) results were obtained. There were no Laboratory Investigations into OOS results or notebook documentation available to explain the re-injection or retesting of in-process, finished product and stability samples which did not meet specifications. The OOS results were not reported and within specification results from reprocessed or re-injected samples were reported on: In-Process Specification, Product Specification and Stability Study Specification Release Reports and Stability Summary Reports. observations.observation_text: An annual report did not include reports of investigations involving chemical or physical properties which, as new information, might affect FDA's previous conclusions about the safety or effectiveness of the drug. Specifically, Annual Reports for ANDA’s that were submitted to FDA did not include out of specification (OOS) results. Only passing data points were submitted. Due to the submission of erroneous data the following ANDA’s were withdrawn. Furthermore, Prior Approval Supplement #004 for ANDA 75-838, Propoxyphene Napsylate and APAP Tablets, 100/650mg, was submitted on 3/16/04 to provide for the discontinuance of Blend Uniformity Testing. This supplement was approved 9/23/04. The test data submitted for Blend Uniformity and Content Uniformity did not contain initial OOS results for a number of batches, only passing results were submitted. Due to the submission of erroneous data the ANDA was withdrawn.

observations.observation_text:
Laboratory records do not include complete data derived from all tests, examinations and assay necessary to assure compliance with established specifications and standards. The QC Laboratory notebooks and binders lacked data from all analytical testing conducted in the QC Laboratory. Laboratory records did not include all data such as out of specification (OOS) results, chromatograms, sample weights, and processing methods. OOS results were substituted with passing results by Analysts and Supervisors. The substitution of data was performed by cutting and pasting of chromatograms, substituting vials, changing sample weights and changing processing methods. For example:
a. For Propoxyphene Napsylate and APAP Tablets, 100/650mg Batch 303110A, chromatogram headers were changed by cutting and pasting, so during review all sample injections would appear to be in sequence, for Dissolution Testing of Tablets D1 and D5.
b. For Propoxyphene Napsylate and APAP Tablets, 100/650mg Batch 104026B Validation Batch, original sample weights were not recorded in the notebook. Sample weights were changed by the analyst until a passing result was obtained for Assay (A2).
c. For Acetaminophen & Codeine Phosphate Tablets, 300/30mg Batch 407148, processing methods were changed by the analyst until the processing method resulted in a passing result. The original processing method was not recorded in the laboratory notebook.

There was no documentation of the number of retests to be performed as required by the SOP. The procedure required retests to be conducted by the original chemist and a second chemist, where the second chemist conducts at least 60% of the tests, or by two chemists, neither of which being the chemist producing the original result. DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES
FOOD AND DRUG ADMINISTRATION
DISTRICT ADDRESS AND PHONE NUMBER
DATE(S) OF INSPECTION
10 Waterview Blvd., 3rd Floor, Parsippany, NJ 07054
(973) 331-4900  Fax: (973) 331-4969
03/10/2026 - 03/21/2026
FEI NUMBER
3018827641
NAME AND TITLE OF INDIVIDUAL TO WHOM REPORT ISSUED
Sandra K. Moretti, Vice President of Quality
FIRM NAME
STREET ADDRESS
Verisynth Pharmaceuticals, Inc.
4200 Crescent Park Drive
CITY, STATE, ZIP CODE
TYPE ESTABLISHMENT INSPECTED
Bridgewater, NJ 08807
Pharmaceutical Drug Manufacturer
This document lists observations made by the FDA representative(s) during the inspection of your facility. They are
inspectional observations, and do not represent a final Agency determination regarding your compliance. If you have an
objection regarding an observation, or have implemented, or plan to implement, corrective action in response to an
observation, you may discuss the objection or action with the FDA representative(s) during the inspection or submit this
information to FDA at the address above.
DURING AN INSPECTION OF YOUR FIRM WE OBSERVED:
OBSERVATION 1
Procedures designed to prevent microbiological contamination of drug products purporting to be sterile were
not established, or if established, not followed.
Specifically, on 03/10/2026, during a walkthrough of Aseptic Fill Suite AF-3 (ISO 5 classified), two operators
(Operator ID: OP-1142 and Operator ID: OP-1198) were observed touching non-classified surfaces —
specifically the exterior of the LAF hood frame (ISO 7 zone) — and immediately thereafter reaching into the ISO
5 critical zone without re-gloving or re-sanitizing. This was observed during the filling of Batch VRP-2026-0311
(Verisynth-A Injection, 50mg/mL, Lot VRP-A-260311).
Additionally, review of aseptic gowning qualification records for OP-1142 shows the most recent gowning
qualification was completed on 01/14/2024 — 24 months prior to the current inspection date. Your firm's SOP
GMP-AS-004 (Aseptic Gowning and Qualification) requires annual re-qualification (every 12 months). A
gowning re-qualification for OP-1142 was not completed within the required timeframe.
OBSERVATION 2
The responsibilities and procedures applicable to the quality control unit were not fully followed.
Specifically, review of Batch Production Record VRP-2026-0289 (Verisynth-B Tablets, 200mg, Lot
VRP-B-260289, manufactured 02/18/2026) revealed the following:

a.
In-process weight variation checks at the 10:15 AM time point show a recorded average tablet weight
of 412.3 mg against a target specification of 400 mg +/- 5% (380 mg – 420 mg). Although within
specification, the QC reviewer initialed this entry without completing the required OOT (out-of-trend)
assessment. Your SOP QC-WGT-011 requires OOT investigation when three consecutive readings
trend toward the specification limit.
b.
The dissolution test result for the 2-hour time point was recorded as 71% against a specification of NLT
75%. This result was below specification. The QC supervisor (QC-SUP-Reinholt) signed the batch
record on 02/20/2026 without initiating an OOS investigation as required by SOP QC-OOS-003. The
batch was released on 02/22/2026.
c.
Environmental monitoring (EM) results for Tablet Compression Suite TC-1 on 02/18/2026 showed a
settle plate count of 12 CFU in the active sampling zone against an alert limit of 5 CFU and an action
limit of 10 CFU. The action limit was exceeded. No corrective action was taken and no investigation
was initiated prior to batch release.
OBSERVATION 3
Laboratory records did not include complete data derived from all tests, examinations, and assays necessary to
assure compliance with established specifications and standards.
Specifically, review of laboratory workbook LW-2026-0044 for Verisynth-A Injection stability testing (Protocol
ST-VRP-A-2024-001, 18-month time point, performed 01/22/2026) identified the following data integrity
concerns:
a.
HPLC sequence file VPRA_STAB_18M_20260122.raw shows injection sequence timestamps for
standard injections at 09:14:32, 09:14:33, and 09:14:35 — three injections within 3 seconds. This is
inconsistent with the instrument's 4-minute equilibration requirement per SOP LAB-HPLC-007 and
indicates the raw data may have been manually entered or overwritten rather than instrument-acquired.
b.
The original printout for the 18-month pH measurement (pH = 6.8, specification 6.5–7.2) contains a
handwritten correction changing the recorded value from '5.8' to '6.8'. The correction is initialed 'JT' but
no date, reason for correction, or supervisor co-signature accompanies the change, as required by
SOP DI-CORR-001.
c.
Analyst training records for Analyst ID LAB-0078 show the analyst is not qualified to perform HPLC
assay testing (qualification completed for UV spectrophotometry only). The 18-month stability HPLC
assay was performed by LAB-0078 without oversight from a qualified analyst.
OBSERVATION 4
Drug product failing to meet established specifications was not rejected.
Specifically, Lot VRP-B-260289 (Verisynth-B Tablets, 200mg) was released for distribution on 02/22/2026,
despite the following out-of-specification (OOS) dissolution result documented in Batch Production Record
VRP-2026-0289:
The 2-hour dissolution time point result of 71% failed the NLT 75% specification established in Product
Specification PS-VRP-B-001 (Rev. 4). No invalidation rationale was documented. No Stage 2 testing was
performed per USP <711>. The Quality Director (QD-Moretti) signed the Certificate of Analysis for Lot
VRP-B-260289 on 02/22/2026 and authorized distribution. As of the first day of this inspection (03/10/2026),

approximately 14,400 units of Lot VRP-B-260289 have been distributed to three distribution centers: NJ-DC-01,
TX-DC-04, and CA-DC-09.

1. PURPOSE
This SOP establishes the requirements for aseptic gowning in ISO-classified cleanroom environments
and the qualification and re-qualification schedule for all personnel performing aseptic operations at
Verisynth Pharmaceuticals, Inc.
2. SCOPE
Applies to all manufacturing, QA, and QC personnel who enter ISO 5, ISO 7, or ISO 8 classified areas
associated with aseptic fill-finish operations (Fill Suites AF-1, AF-2, AF-3, and Buffer Preparation Suite
BP-1).
3. GOWNING QUALIFICATION REQUIREMENTS
3.1 Initial Qualification: All personnel must complete initial gowning qualification before performing
unsupervised aseptic operations. Qualification consists of three consecutive successful media fill
observations evaluated by a QA representative.
3.2 Re-qualification Frequency: All qualified aseptic personnel must complete annual
re-qualification (every 12 months) from the date of their most recent qualification. Re-qualification
records are maintained in the Personnel Qualification Database (PQD) and reviewed monthly by QA.
3.3 Re-qualification Failure: Personnel whose re-qualification has lapsed are immediately suspended
from aseptic operations until re-qualification is completed and documented. QA must be notified within
24 hours of any lapsed qualification.
4. GOWNING PROCEDURE — ISO 5 ENTRY (CRITICAL ZONE)
Step 1:
Don sterile gloves (inner pair) in the ISO 7 anteroom.
Step 2:
Enter gowning room. Don sterile coverall, hood, and face mask.
Step 3:
Don sterile boot covers (sterile, ISO 5 grade).
Step 4:
Don outer sterile gloves. Sanitize with 70% IPA.
Step 5:
Pass through airlock into ISO 5 fill suite. Do not touch non-classified surfaces after donning
outer gloves.

Step 6:
If any non-classified surface contact occurs (ISO 7 frame, door handle, non-sterile
equipment): EXIT the critical zone, remove outer gloves, don new sterile outer gloves,
re-sanitize, and re-enter.
Step 7:
Document gowning in the Gowning Log (Form GMP-AS-004-F1) with operator ID, date,
time, and sanitization confirmation.

INST-TMP-014 (Autoclave Temp Recorder) was used for sterilization cycle validation records for autoclave cycles AC-2026-0044 through AC-2026-0061 during the period 02/04/2026 through 03/10/2026, while past its calibration due date.
observations.source_notes_excerpt: Instruments, apparatus, gauges, and recording devices used in manufacturing, processing, packing, or holding of a drug product were not calibrated according to an established written program containing specific directions, schedules, limits for accuracy and precision, and provisions for remedial action when accuracy and precision limits were not met.

2/12
The quality control unit lacks authority to fully investigate errors that have occurred.
The Quality Unit and Senior Management failed to assure all drug products distributed have the safety, identity, quality, and purity
that they are represented to possess. The Quality Unit failed to: review electronic data as part of batch release, review computer
audit trails in the Waters Empower Data Acquisition System and provide adequate training to analytical chemists. These practices
led to the Quality Unit releasing batches of drug products which failed to meet in­process, finished product and stability
specifications. These practices also led to the submission of erroneous data in Annual Reports and Prior Approval Supplement #
004, for ANDA 75­838, which requested discontinuance of Blend Uniformity testing for Propoxyphene Napsylate and
Acetaminophen 100mg/650 mg Tablets. The lack of Quality oversight resulted in: the ceasing of manufacturing on 5/13/05
5/19/05, the ceasing of distribution of all drug products on 5/26/05 5/13/05, the recall of all batches (3,184) of drug products and
the withdrawal of at least five Abbreviated New Drug Applications.
 
OBSERVATION 2
Drug products failing to meet established standards, specifications, and quality control criteria are not rejected.
Samples of drug products were routinely resampled, and re­injected or reprocessed in the [REDACTION] 
System during testing in the QC Laboratory when out of specification (OOS) results were obtained. There were no Laboratory
Investigations into OOS results or notebook documentation available to explain the re­injection or retesting of in­process, finished
product and stability samples which did not meet specifications. The OOS results were not reported and within specification
results from reprocessed or re­injected samples were reported on: In­Process Specification, Product Specification and Stability
Study Specification Release Reports and Stability Summary Reports.
 
Examples of drug products which were released with OOS values are listed below.

OBSERVATION 7
Written records are not made of investigations into unexplained discrepancies and the failure of a batch or any of its components
to meet specifications.
Laboratory investigations were not conducted when out of specification (OOS) results were generated during in­process, finished
product and stability testing of drug products. Examples of batches where OOS results were generated and not investigated are
included in FDA­483, point # 2. Quality Control Procedure, SOP # QC­021­06, Acceptance/Rejection Criteria for OOS Analytical
Test Results, requires an investigation be conducted when OOS results are generated.
 
OBSERVATION 8
Employees are not given training in current good manufacturing practices and written procedures required by current good
manufacturing practice regulations.
QC Laboratory analysts were not routinely trained in Quality Control procedures such as SOP # QC­011­03, Laboratory Deviation
Investigations and SOP # QC­021­06, Acceptance/Rejection Criteria for OOS Analytical Test Results. This lack of training and
oversight by management contributed to the non­reporting of OOS results in the QC Laboratory.
 
OBSERVATION 9
Written records of investigations into unexplained discrepancies and the failure of a batch or any of its components to meet
specifications do not always include the conclusions and followup.
OOS Investigation # 04­00S­031, for Methylphenidate HCl ER Tablets 20 mg 18 month stability lot 303087A was initiated due to
dissolution failing results. The specification required the average of 24 tablets to be within the range of [REDACTION] at the L3, 1
hour dissolution time point. The average of the 24 tablets was reported to be 48.4% with a minimum result of 45.8% and a
maximum of 50.2%. The investigation was found to be incomplete. The investigation concluded that the original failing results
were invalid due to an analyst technique issue. There was no documentation provided within the investigation or within the analyst
notebook to justify invalidating the failing dissolution results. Although corrective measures were identified in the investigation,
there was no documentation to show that the corrective measures had been completed. Additionally, there was no review of data
acquired by the same analysts for the same tests for other lots of the same product.

OBSERVATION 11
Established laboratory control mechanisms are not followed.
a. An Investigation was not issued prior to any retesting for Lot 303087B, Methylphenidate HCl ER 18M stability lot, as required
by procedure SOP # QC­011­03, Laboratory Deviation Investigation. Lot 303087B, Methylphenidate HCl ER Tablets 20 mg,
18M Dissolution stability analysis found that the original L3 testing results were within specification. Two months after the
analysis of 24 tablets for Lot 303087B for 18M stability, 6 more tablets were tested. The results from the final analysis of the 6
tablets were reported as 18 M Dissolution results.
b. SOP # QC­006­01 Retesting and Resampling Analytical Control Laboratory, effective 8/27/03 was not followed for
Methylphenidate HCl ER18M stability lot 303087A:
1. There was no documentation of the number of retests to be performed as required by the SOP. The SOP required the
number of retest to be documented prior to initiating testing to establish a definite limit beyond which no additional testing
would be permitted.
2. The procedure required retests to be conducted by the original chemist and a second chemist, where the second
chemist conducts at least 60% of the tests, or by two chemists, neither of which being the chemist producing the original
result. Retests were not carried out by the original chemist and a second chemist. Additionally, the test was not carried
out by two chemists other than the original chemist.
3. Investigation 04­OOS­031, initiated 12/8/04 and completed 2/18/05, exceeded 30 working days. The procedure required
investigations to be completed in a brief time frame not to exceed 30 working days from the start of the investigation.

OBSERVATION 12
Control procedures are not established which validate the performance of those manufacturing processes that may be
responsible for causing variability in the characteristics of in­process material and the drug product.
a. There is no assurance that results for in­process physical testing are recorded accurately. For example, the Pre­Validation
batch record (TB­110) for Hydrocodone Bitartrate and Acetaminophen Tablets, USP 5mg/325mg shows the specification for
tablet thickness range as 0.308” to 0.358”; this range was crossed out and the correct range of [REDACTION] was
handwritten in the batch record. The in­process tablet thickness results show all tablets were within the corrected thickness
specification of [REDACTION] during compression on 10/15/01. The Research and Development (R&D) In­Process Data
Sheet shows the thickness of 60 tablets to be within a thickness range of 0.330” and 0.334” which corresponds to the tablet
thickness specification which was incorrectly written on the Master Batch Record. Retains from this batch were tested on
6/10/05, and the results show the thickness of the tablets were between [REDACTION] , which was the correct specification
that was handwritten on the Master Batch Record.
b. Manufacturing Investigations into rejected batches of drug products did not include an evaluation of the validated
manufacturing process. For example, seven of nine batches (78%) of Methylphenidate ER 20 mg Tablets, manufactured
between May 2003 and November 2004 were investigated in the laboratory, due to initial OOS results or out of trend results.
Two of the seven lab investigations, resulted in the rejection of batches 411021 and 310004. Manufacturing Investigations,
04­008, for batch 310004, and Manufacturing Investigation 05­001, for batch, 411021 did not include an evaluation of the
validated manufacturing process for Methylphenidate ER 20 mg Tablets.
c. There is no assurance that manufacturing processes for drug products are validated in that out of specification (OOS) results
were generated, but not reported. Several examples are listed below.
